objects.description: Opaque integer array helper for language bindings. Note: actual structure is not defined; returned as plain int pointer.

Dynamically growing array container for fixed-size elements. Stores bookkeeping for element size, growth increment, count, allocated capacity, and backing storage in chunk pointers. Elements are copied into internal storage; element_at returns a pointer to internal memory owned by the array. Creation via icalarray_new; release with icalarray_free. Sorting supported via user-supplied compare. Set/append copy bytes from provided element pointer; callers must manage any heap members of their elements when overwriting or freeing.

objects.definition: typedef void (*icalattach_free_fn_t)(char *data, void *user_data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a deallocator callback associated with an icalattach created from in-memory data. The callback receives the data pointer and a user_data pointer. The documentation notes it is currently not used; pass a suitable function when using icalattach_new_from_data if needed by future versions.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalcomponent_impl icalcomponent;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a calendar component (VCALENDAR, VEVENT, VTODO, etc.). The actual structure is defined privately; users manage it via the API. Construct with icalcomponent_new(), clone with icalcomponent_clone(), destroy with icalcomponent_free(). Components can own subcomponents and properties; parent/child relations are maintained by add/remove APIs. Validity can be checked with icalcomponent_is_valid().

External iterator for traversing child icalcomponent objects of a given kind within a parent component. Initialized by icalcomponent_begin_component()/icalcomponent_end_component(), advanced with icalcompiter_next()/icalcompiter_prior(), and dereferenced to the current component with icalcompiter_deref(). Callers should treat the layout as an implementation detail though it is exposed to avoid heap allocation.

External iterator for traversing icalproperty objects of a given kind within an icalcomponent. Created by icalcomponent_begin_property(), advanced with icalpropiter_next(), and dereferenced with icalpropiter_deref(). Exposed to avoid dynamic allocation; treat as opaque.

objects.definition: typedef void *(*icalmemory_malloc_f)(size_t);

objects.definition: typedef void (*icalmemory_free_f)(void *);

Opaque parameter object representing a property parameter in iCalendar. This header only declares functions that operate on icalparameter; the concrete struct definition is not present here (it is declared in icalderivedparameter.h). Instances are created with icalparameter_new(), icalparameter_new_from_string(), or icalparameter_new_from_value_string(), can be cloned with icalparameter_clone(), and must be destroyed with icalparameter_free().

objects.definition: typedef struct icalparser_impl icalparser;

Create with icalparser_new() and destroy with icalparser_free().
Enumeration describing the parser’s current state: error, success, beginning or end of a component, or in-progress. Used by icalparser_get_state() and for error signaling during parsing.

objects.definition: typedef char *(*icalparser_line_gen_func)(char *s, size_t size, void *d);
objects.description: Function-pointer type for caller-supplied line generators that fill a buffer with one content line and return it, or return NULL on EOF/error. The third argument d is user data set via icalparser_set_gen_data().

Enumeration controlling how the parser handles CONTROL characters in content lines: keep them, omit them, or treat as an error (insert X-LIC-ERROR). Access via icalparser_get_ctrl() and icalparser_set_ctrl().

Represents a period of time in iCalendar: either a start/end pair or a start plus a duration. Members are other libical types (icaltimetype and icaldurationtype). Initialization macro ICALPERIODTYPE_INITIALIZER is provided in this header. Details about icaltimetype and icaldurationtype are defined in their respective headers.

Opaque handle to an iCalendar property object. Only referenced here; the concrete definition is not present in this header. Managed through the creation, cloning, and free functions declared here. Instances own icalparameter and icalvalue children via the provided APIs.

objects.definition: /* incomplete type; only referenced via pointer in this header */

Opaque handle to an iCalendar parameter object. Only referenced here; not defined in this header. Parameters can be added to or removed from an icalproperty and queried for parentage.

Enumeration identifying the kind of an icalparameter. Only referenced here; defined elsewhere. Used for filtering and removal APIs.

Enumeration of STATUS values. Only referenced; defined elsewhere. String conversion helpers are declared.
Enumeration of ACTION values. Only referenced; defined elsewhere. String conversion helpers are declared.
Enumeration of TRANSP values. Only referenced; defined elsewhere. String conversion helpers are declared.
Enumeration of CLASS values. Only referenced; defined elsewhere. String conversion helpers are declared.
Enumeration of PARTICIPANT-TYPE values. Only referenced; defined elsewhere. String conversion helpers are declared.
Enumeration of RESOURCE-TYPE values. Only referenced; defined elsewhere. String conversion helpers are declared.

objects.definition: typedef icalarray icalstrarray;
objects.description: Alias type for icalarray specialized to hold pointers to C strings (char *) via helper APIs/macros in this header. It represents a dynamically resizable array whose elements are strings owned by the array. Construction is via the icalstrarray_new macro (wrapping icalarray_new with element size sizeof(char *)). Free with icalstrarray_free(). Unknown internal structure because icalarray is defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: typedef struct _icaltimezone icaltimezone;
objects.description: Opaque timezone type forward-declared here to break circular dependencies. No layout is visible in this header; it is used to tag an icaltimetype with its native timezone or to pass zones to conversion functions. Details of construction, lifetime, and internals are unknown from this header.

Represents a half-open interval of time in UTC with a busy/free flag. start and end are in seconds since the Unix epoch (icaltime_t). is_busy indicates whether the interval is considered busy (1) or free (0).

A pseudo-object encapsulating either a DATE or DATE-TIME, optionally bound to a native timezone. When is_date==1 only the date fields are meaningful. For DATE-TIME, time fields and zone are relevant; zone==NULL denotes a floating time. is_daylight flags daylight saving status when applicable.

objects.definition: #define icaltime_t time_t
objects.description: Alias macro to the C library time_t used throughout this header for epoch-second values. As a macro definition, it is not a real typedef; pointer form shown for consistency. Construction/destruction semantics are those of time_t.

objects.definition: typedef struct _icaltimezone icaltimezone;
objects.description: Opaque timezone handle used throughout libical’s timezone API. The actual struct layout is hidden; it is forward-declared here to break circular dependencies. Instances are created, copied, and freed via the provided API. Treat as non-POD and manage exclusively through functions in this header/library. Ownership: callers that obtain a new or copied icaltimezone must free it with icaltimezone_free(). Many accessors return non-owning pointers/strings whose lifetime is tied to the library or the icaltimezone instance.

Holds either a specific time (icaltimetype) or a time period (icalperiodtype) for date-time/period value representations used in iCalendar contexts. The union-like pairing allows consumers to carry both forms; semantics depend on usage in calling APIs. Details of icaltimetype and icalperiodtype are defined elsewhere.

Stores geographic coordinates as fixed-size character arrays for latitude and longitude. Each field is a string buffer of length ICAL_GEO_LEN (16). Formatting and range validation are external to this type.

Represents an alarm trigger as either an absolute time (time) or a relative duration (duration). Only one of the fields is typically meaningful at a time; interpretation depends on higher-level alarm/property logic. The embedded types are defined elsewhere.

Encapsulates an iTIP/iCalendar request-status value: a status code (icalrequeststatus enum from included headers), a human-readable description (points to static library data; do not free), and an optional debug string owned by an icalvalue (do not free manually).

Policy enum controlling how libical handles unknown tokens (currently affects parameters): treat as IANA-registered, discard, or treat as error. The typedef name ical_unknown_token_handling aliases the enum.

Opaque value object for iCalendar property values. This header only declares functions that operate on icalvalue; the actual struct/type definition is not present here (it is likely defined in icalvalueimpl.h or another internal header). Treat as an opaque handle managed via the provided API.
Enumeration type identifying the kind of an icalvalue (e.g., text, integer, date, etc.). The enum definition is not in this header; it is referenced for APIs that create, query, and validate kinds.
Enumeration used to represent comparison results between two icalvalue objects (e.g., equal, not equal, none). The concrete enum definition is not present in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalpvl_list_t *icalpvl_list;
objects.description: Opaque pointer type representing an internal list container used by libical. The underlying struct icalpvl_list_t is not defined in this header, so the type is opaque; it likely manages a doubly-linked list of icalpvl_elem nodes storing void* payloads.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalpvl_elem_t *icalpvl_elem;
objects.description: Opaque pointer type representing an internal list element (node) in the libical private list (pvl). The underlying struct icalpvl_elem_t is not defined here; nodes likely form a doubly-linked list and store a void* data payload.

objects.definition: typedef int (*icalpvl_comparef)(void *a, void *b);
objects.description: Function pointer type for comparison callbacks used to order insertions into an icalpvl_list. Returns an int comparison result; exact contract (e.g., negative/zero/positive) is not documented here.

objects.definition: typedef int (*icalpvl_findf)(void *a, void *b);
objects.description: Function pointer type for predicate callbacks used to find elements within an icalpvl_list. Should return nonzero when the element matches. Parameter a is a list element’s data (as void*), b is user data.

objects.definition: typedef void (*icalpvl_applyf)(void *a, void *b);
objects.description: Function pointer type for per-element callbacks applied across an icalpvl_list. Parameter a is a list element’s data (as void*), b is user data. The function returns no value.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalgauge_impl icalgauge;
objects.description: Opaque handle for an iCal component filter ("gauge"). Constructed from an SQL-like expression and used to test whether components match. Actual struct layout is hidden.

Abstract base type representing a collection of iCal components with a vtable for different storage backends (file, directory, DB). The struct definition shown is the implementation/vtable; instances are created via factory functions and subclass initializers.
Enumeration of icalset backend kinds: file-based, directory-based, or Berkeley DB-based.
External iterator over an icalset, optionally filtered by an icalgauge and tracking recurrence iteration state. Contains iteration cursors and timezone context.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalcluster_impl icalcluster;
objects.description: Opaque container representing a cluster of components grouped under a key (e.g., by time period). Provides mutation and iteration of contained components with change tracking.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalfileset_impl icalfileset;
objects.description: Opaque concrete icalset backend that stores components in a single file (cluster). Managed through the icalset interface and dedicated helper APIs.
Options struct for opening/initializing an icalfileset, including file flags, mode, locking behavior, and an optional initial cluster.

objects.definition: typedef struct icaldirset_impl icaldirset;
objects.description: Opaque concrete icalset backend that stores components across multiple files in a directory, grouped (typically) by DTSTAMP month/year into clusters.
Options struct for opening/initializing an icaldirset; currently only open() flags are specified.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalcalendar_impl icalcalendar;
objects.description: Opaque type representing a filesystem-backed calendar composed of multiple icalsets (booked, incoming, properties, freebusy) with optional locking semantics.
Concrete structure encapsulating a collection of free/busy time spans computed over a period. Stores a list of busy spans and the overall start/end bounds.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalcalendar_impl icalcalendar;
objects.description: Opaque calendar handle for storing calendar data in a filesystem-backed store. The underlying struct icalcalendar_impl is intentionally hidden; clients manage lifetimes via the provided API. The calendar aggregates multiple icalset collections: booked, incoming, properties, and free/busy. Implementation details are not exposed in this header.
Enumeration type representing the X-LIC-CLASS property classification used by libical. It is only referenced here as a return type; the actual enum/typedef definition is not present in this header.
Opaque/libical component handle representing an iCalendar component (VEVENT, VTODO, etc.). Only referenced here; not defined in this header.
Opaque/libical set handle representing a collection of iCalendar components. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalcluster_impl icalcluster;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a cluster object that associates a key with an icalcomponent tree and provides change tracking and iteration utilities. The actual structure is hidden (forward-declared as struct icalcluster_impl), making this a handle type managed through the provided API.

objects.definition: typedef struct icaldirset_impl icaldirset;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for a directory-based icalset backend. It aliases an internal struct icaldirset_impl that is not defined in this header. Instances are created and managed via the icaldirset_* API and used through the icalset interface functions. The underlying structure details are intentionally hidden.

Options struct for configuring icaldirset behavior when opening/initializing a store. Currently contains an open(2)-style flags field (e.g., O_RDONLY, O_RDWR). Passed via the options_in parameter to icaldirset_init (cast to void* by the API); exact interpretation may be backend-specific.

Implementation struct backing an icaldirset, storing the directory path, options, and state for iterating and filtering components via a gauge and cluster. Exact semantics of first_component, directory, and directory_iterator are not fully documented here.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalfileset_impl icalfileset;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a fileset-based icalset implementation. The underlying struct icalfileset_impl is not defined in this header, making icalfileset an opaque type used to represent a file-backed calendar set internals. Lifecycle is managed via icalset/icalfileset API functions. Details of its contents are intentionally hidden.

Options struct for opening/configuring an icalfileset via icalset_new()/icalfileset_init. Fields: flags (passed to open(), e.g., O_RDONLY), mode (file permissions for creation), safe_saves (nonzero to enable locking/safer saves), cluster (optional icalcluster to seed data). icalfileset_options_default provides library defaults.

Concrete implementation struct for an ical fileset. It embeds a parent icalset (super), stores the filesystem path and options used to create the set, and maintains runtime state such as the current component cluster, an optional gauge for filtering, a change flag, and an open file descriptor. Details of lifecycle and ownership semantics are not documented here; fields reference external types defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalgauge_impl icalgauge;
objects.description: Opaque gauge type used to filter icalcomponent objects based on an SQL-like expression. The actual structure (struct icalgauge_impl) is intentionally hidden; this header provides only a typedef to enforce opacity. Instances are created from an SQL string and can be queried for their expand setting, used to compare against components, dumped for debugging, and freed when no longer needed.

objects.definition:
typedef enum icalgaugecompare
{
    ICALGAUGECOMPARE_EQUAL = ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_EQUAL,
    ICALGAUGECOMPARE_LESS = ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_LESS,
    ICALGAUGECOMPARE_LESSEQUAL = ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_LESSEQUAL,
    ICALGAUGECOMPARE_GREATER = ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_GREATER,
    ICALGAUGECOMPARE_GREATEREQUAL = ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_GREATEREQUAL,
    ICALGAUGECOMPARE_NOTEQUAL = ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_NOTEQUAL,
    ICALGAUGECOMPARE_REGEX = ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_REGEX,
    ICALGAUGECOMPARE_ISNULL = ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_ISNULL,
    ICALGAUGECOMPARE_ISNOTNULL = ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_ISNOTNULL,
    ICALGAUGECOMPARE_NONE = 0
} icalgaugecompare;
objects.description: Comparator enum for gauge filtering; maps to X-LIC compare types (equal, relational, regex, null/not-null). Values mirror external ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_* constants. Used to express how a property should be compared in a where-clause.
Logical operator enum for combining gauge where-clauses (none/and/or).

Predicate specification for a gauge filter: identifies component and property to test, the comparison operation, an optional value string, and the boolean logic connector to adjacent predicates. Types icalcomponent_kind, icalproperty_kind are referenced from included headers and not defined here.

Internal representation of an ical gauge (query). Holds PVL lists for select/from/where clauses and an expand flag. The list element types are described by comments; actual icalpvl_list comes from external headers and is not defined here.

objects.definition: typedef struct icalset_impl icalset;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a collection of iCalendar components. It is a typedef to an internal implementation struct (icalset_impl). Instances are created via the provided factory functions and represent sets stored in files, directories, or databases. Details of the structure are hidden; manage through the API only.
Enumeration specifying the backing store/type for an icalset: single file, directory of files, or Berkeley DB. Used when constructing an icalset.

External iterator state used to traverse components in an icalset, optionally filtered by a gauge and expanded over recurrences, with timezone context. Treat as an opaque-by-convention value object; use the icalsetiter_* API to operate it.

Concrete implementation vtable and data for an icalset. Contains type tag, data source name, and a suite of function pointers that implement set operations and iteration. Library users normally interact with the opaque alias icalset; this struct is for implementers of new backing stores.

Opaque-style struct that represents a collection of free/busy time spans over a period. It stores a list of icaltime_span entries plus the overall start and end bounds as icaltimetype values. Used to compute free/busy, dump contents, produce VFREEBUSY components, and create occupancy matrices. Internal field types (icalpvl_list, icaltimetype) are defined elsewhere.

objects.definition:
enum yytokentype
{
    STRING = 258,
    SELECT = 259,
    FROM = 260,
    WHERE = 261,
    COMMA = 262,
    QUOTE = 263,
    EQUALS = 264,
    NOTEQUALS = 265,
    LESS = 266,
    GREATER = 267,
    LESSEQUALS = 268,
    GREATEREQUALS = 269,
    AND = 270,
    OR = 271,
    EOL = 272,
    END = 273,
    IS = 274,
    NOT = 275,
    SQLNULL = 276
};
objects.description: Token enumeration generated by Bison for a SQL-like grammar. Enumerators represent terminal symbols returned by the lexer to the parser.

Bison semantic value type for parser symbols. Here it's a union currently holding a single member v_string for string token values. The alias yystype is provided for backward compatibility. Construction is typically performed by the lexer by assigning to sslval (the extern semantic value) or yylval in standard setups.

Defaults container for vCalendar-to-iCalendar conversion. Provides fallback values for alarm properties (audio URL, format type, and description) when missing in the source vCalendar data. Owns three C strings; allocation and lifetime are managed by the caller.

Referenced type representing an iCalendar component. Not defined in this header; definition resides in icalcomponent.h. Included here because functions in this header return it, but it is not defined in this file.

Referenced vCalendar object type used as input to conversion functions. Not defined in this header; definition resides in vobject.h. Included here because it appears in function signatures, but it is not defined here.

Opaque type representing a vCalendar object node, used throughout libical’s vCal/vCard compatibility layer. This header only references VObject; its actual definition is not present here and is expected to be provided by included headers (likely vcc.h). Without the definition, details such as fields, lifetime management, and ownership semantics are unknown from this file alone.

objects.definition: typedef void (*MimeErrorHandler) (const char *);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a MIME error callback. The callback receives a C string describing an error encountered during MIME parsing. Details about invocation timing and threading are not specified here.
Opaque type representing a vCard/vCalendar object used by the parsing API. It is referenced here but defined elsewhere (likely in vobject.h).

objects.definition: typedef struct VObject VObject;
objects.description: Opaque vCard/vCalendar node object representing either a component, a property, or a value container in the vObject tree. The actual structure is intentionally hidden; use the provided API functions to create, manipulate, iterate, serialize, and destroy instances.
Concrete iterator used to traverse child properties of a VObject. Holds iteration state (start and next pointers). Initialize with initPropIterator and advance with nextVObject/moreIteration.

functions.name: icaltime_null_time
functions.description: Constructor returning an icaltimetype representing a null time (no time set), which corresponds to the beginning of the epoch.

functions.name: icaltime_null_date
functions.description: Constructor returning an icaltimetype representing a null date (no time set).

functions.name: icaltime_current_time_with_zone
functions.description: Returns the current time as an icaltimetype in the given timezone.
requirements: zone: pointer to a timezone; behavior for NULL is not specified in the header.

functions.name: icaltime_today
functions.description: Returns the current day as an icaltimetype with is_date set (DATE value).

functions.name: icaltime_from_timet_with_zone
functions.signature: struct icaltimetype icaltime_from_timet_with_zone(icaltime_t tm, bool is_date, const icaltimezone *zone)
functions.description: Constructs an icaltimetype from seconds past the UNIX epoch with optional DATE flag and timezone. If is_date is true, the returned value is a DATE; if zone is NULL, the result is a floating time; if zone is provided (UTC or otherwise), it is stored as the native zone.
requirements: tm: seconds since UNIX epoch.
is_date: 1/true to create a DATE, 0/false for DATE-TIME.
zone: NULL for floating time; non-NULL to set the native timezone on the result.

functions.name: icaltime_from_string
functions.description: Parses an RFC5545-compliant DATE-TIME string (ISO-8601-2004 forms), including local, UTC (with trailing Z), or TZID-prefixed local time, and returns the corresponding icaltimetype.
requirements: str must be a valid DATE-TIME in one of the documented forms (e.g., 19980118T230000, 19980119T070000Z, or TZID=Area/Location:... ).

functions.name: icaltime_from_day_of_year
functions.signature: struct icaltimetype icaltime_from_day_of_year(int doy, int year)
functions.description: Constructs an icaltimetype from a day-of-year and year. Jan 1 is day 1 (not 0).
requirements: doy counts from 1 (Jan 1 = 1).

functions.name: icaltime_as_timet
functions.description: Returns seconds since the UNIX epoch for the given time. No timezone conversion is performed; callers should only pass UTC times. Range depends on size of time_t (64-bit: 1902-01-01 to <10000-01-01; 32-bit: up to <2038-01-18).
requirements: Pass a time in UTC; no conversion to UTC is performed by this function.

functions.name: icaltime_as_timet_with_zone
functions.signature: icaltime_t icaltime_as_timet_with_zone(struct icaltimetype tt, const icaltimezone *zone)
functions.description: Returns seconds since the UNIX epoch for the given time, after first converting the value to the specified timezone. If zone is NULL, no conversion is done and the time is returned in its native timezone.
requirements: If zone is NULL, the result uses the time's native timezone.

functions.name: icaltime_as_ical_string
functions.description: Formats an icaltimetype to an RFC5545-compliant string. The returned buffer is owned by libical.
requirements: Caller must not free the returned string; it may be invalidated by subsequent library calls.

functions.name: icaltime_as_ical_string_r
functions.description: Formats an icaltimetype to an RFC5545-compliant string. The returned buffer is owned by the caller.
requirements: Caller must free the returned string with the appropriate deallocator (e.g., icalmemory_free_buffer()).

functions.name: icaltime_get_timezone
functions.description: Returns the timezone associated with the given icaltimetype, or NULL for floating/none.

functions.name: icaltime_get_tzid
functions.description: Returns the tzid string for the given icaltimetype, or NULL if it is a floating time.

functions.name: icaltime_set_timezone
functions.signature: struct icaltimetype icaltime_set_timezone(struct icaltimetype *t, const icaltimezone *zone)
functions.description: Reinterprets the given icaltime relative to another timezone without applying offset adjustments (not a conversion). If t is DATE, timezone is not modified and a copy is returned. For actual timezone conversion, use icaltime_convert_to_zone.
requirements: t must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
If t is of type DATE, the timezone is not changed and the returned value equals the input.

functions.name: icaltime_day_of_year
functions.description: Returns the day of the year for the given time, counting from 1 (Jan 1st).

functions.name: icaltime_day_of_week
functions.description: Returns the day of the week for the given time, where Sunday=1 through Saturday=7.

functions.name: icaltime_start_doy_week
functions.signature: int icaltime_start_doy_week(struct icaltimetype t, int fdow)
functions.description: Returns the day-of-year for the first day of the week containing the given time. Documentation describes Sunday as week start; fdow parameter indicates first day-of-week.
requirements: fdow indicates first day of week (exact accepted range not specified in header).

functions.name: icaltime_is_null_time
functions.description: Returns true if the time is a null time (indicating no time has been set).

functions.name: icaltime_is_valid_time
functions.description: Returns false if the time fields are clearly invalid (but not null). Typically occurs with uninitialized or improperly set fields.

functions.name: icaltime_is_date
functions.description: Returns true if the time is a DATE (as opposed to a DATE-TIME).

functions.name: icaltime_is_utc
functions.description: Returns true if the time is relative to the UTC timezone. Note: Implementation may only check the zone.

functions.name: icaltime_compare
functions.signature: int icaltime_compare(struct icaltimetype a, struct icaltimetype b)
functions.description: Compares two times by converting both to UTC and returning -1, 0, or 1 if a<b, a==b, or a>b respectively.

functions.name: icaltime_compare_date_only
functions.signature: int icaltime_compare_date_only(struct icaltimetype a, struct icaltimetype b)
functions.description: Compares two icaltimetypes using only their DATE parts after converting to UTC; returns -1, 0, or 1.

functions.name: icaltime_compare_date_only_tz
functions.signature: int icaltime_compare_date_only_tz(struct icaltimetype a, struct icaltimetype b, icaltimezone *tz)
functions.description: Compares the DATE parts of two times in the specified timezone; returns -1, 0, or 1.
requirements: tz: timezone in which to perform the comparison (not documented as optional).

functions.name: icaltime_adjust
functions.signature: void icaltime_adjust(struct icaltimetype *tt, int days, int hours, int minutes, int seconds)
functions.description: Adds (or subtracts) the specified offset to an icaltimetype in-place using days, hours, minutes, and seconds.
requirements: tt must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.

functions.name: icaltime_normalize
functions.description: Normalizes an icaltimetype so all components are within their normal ranges (e.g., minutes=70 becomes minutes=10, hour+=1).

functions.name: icaltime_convert_to_zone
functions.signature: struct icaltimetype icaltime_convert_to_zone(struct icaltimetype tt, icaltimezone *zone)
functions.description: Converts an icaltimetype from its native timezone to the specified timezone, updating the timezone field. DATE values are returned unchanged; floating times are reinterpreted relative to the target zone.
requirements: zone must be a valid timezone pointer (behavior for NULL not defined in header).
DATE inputs are not converted; output equals input.

functions.name: icaltime_days_in_month
functions.description: Returns the number of days in the given month of the specified year.
requirements: month expected in 1..12 (not explicitly stated, but implied by struct semantics).

functions.name: icaltime_is_leap_year
functions.description: Returns whether the specified year is a leap year (year is the full year, e.g., 2001).

functions.name: icaltime_days_in_year
functions.description: Returns the number of days in the specified year.

functions.name: icaltime_span_new
functions.signature: struct icaltime_span icaltime_span_new(struct icaltimetype dtstart, struct icaltimetype dtend, bool is_busy)
functions.description: Creates an icaltime_span with the given start, end, and busy flag. The resulting span times are in UTC.
requirements: dtstart and dtend represent the beginning and end of the span; documented as specified in UTC.

functions.name: icaltime_span_overlaps
functions.description: Returns true if two spans overlap (including equality), and false if they are merely adjacent or disjoint.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be non-NULL pointers to valid spans.

functions.name: icaltime_span_contains
functions.description: Returns true if span s is fully contained within span container.
requirements: s and container must be non-NULL pointers to valid spans.

functions.name: icaldurationtype_from_seconds
functions.description: Constructs an icaldurationtype from an integer count of seconds. Negative input sets is_neg=1 and seconds stored as absolute value. Does not refactor into days/hours/minutes.
requirements: Input seconds may be negative or positive; function sets is_neg accordingly
Returned struct is a value type; no allocation to free

functions.name: icaldurationtype_from_string
functions.description: Parses an RFC5545 duration string into an icaldurationtype (e.g. +PT05M). On malformed input, sets icalerrno=ICAL_MALFORMEDDATA_ERROR and returns a bad duration.
requirements: str must point to a NUL-terminated string; passing NULL sets error and returns bad duration
Caller should check icaldurationtype_is_bad_duration() on return and/or icalerrno

functions.name: icaldurationtype_as_seconds
functions.description: Converts an icaldurationtype to signed seconds. Returns a negative value if the duration points backward in time.
requirements: If duration has non-zero days or weeks, this is considered an error condition (conversion only uses hours/minutes/seconds)

functions.name: icaldurationtype_as_ical_string
functions.description: Formats a duration as an RFC5545 string. The returned string is owned by the caller and must be freed with icalmemory_free_buffer().
requirements: Caller must free the returned buffer with icalmemory_free_buffer()
d must be a valid duration struct

functions.name: icaldurationtype_as_ical_string_r
functions.description: Formats a duration as an RFC5545 string. The returned string is owned by libical and must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: Returned pointer is transient library-owned; do not free or store long-term

functions.name: icaldurationtype_null_duration
functions.description: Creates a zero-length icaldurationtype (all fields zero, is_neg=0).
requirements: Value type; no allocation or freeing required

functions.name: icaldurationtype_bad_duration
functions.description: Returns a sentinel icaldurationtype indicating an error condition (used by parsers).
requirements: Value type; check with icaldurationtype_is_bad_duration() before use

functions.name: icaldurationtype_is_null_duration
functions.description: Returns true if the duration is zero-length.
requirements: d must be a valid struct; no side effects

functions.name: icaldurationtype_is_bad_duration
functions.description: Returns true if the duration is marked as a bad/error duration.
requirements: Use to validate results from parsers before use

functions.name: icalduration_extend
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT struct icaltimetype icalduration_extend(struct icaltimetype t,                                                            struct icaldurationtype d);
functions.description: Adds a duration to a time and returns the resulting icaltimetype.
requirements: t should be initialized icaltimetype
d should be a valid duration; adding may overflow fields until normalized by internal logic

functions.name: icalduration_from_times
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT struct icaldurationtype icalduration_from_times(struct icaltimetype t1,                                                                    struct icaltimetype t2);
functions.description: Computes the duration (t2 - t1) as an icaldurationtype.
requirements: t1 and t2 should be valid times; timezone handling follows libical’s icaltimetype semantics

functions.name: icalperiodtype_from_string
functions.description: Parses a period string into an icalperiodtype. Supports formats START/END and START/DURATION; times are RFC5545 strings. On malformed input sets icalerrno=ICAL_MALFORMEDDATA_ERROR and returns a null period.
requirements: str must be non-NULL and RFC5545 compliant; otherwise caller must check icalerrno and/or icalperiodtype_is_null_period()

functions.name: icalperiodtype_as_ical_string
functions.description: Formats a period as an iCal string. The returned pointer is owned by libical; do not free.
requirements: On allocation error sets icalerrno=ICAL_ALLOCATION_ERROR
Do not free or modify returned memory

functions.name: icalperiodtype_as_ical_string_r
functions.description: Formats a period as an iCal string. The returned buffer is owned by the caller and must be freed appropriately (e.g., icalmemory_free_buffer()).
requirements: Caller must free the returned string
On allocation error sets icalerrno=ICAL_ALLOCATION_ERROR

functions.name: icalperiodtype_null_period
functions.description: Returns a null/empty icalperiodtype (start, end null time; duration null).
requirements: Value type; no allocation

functions.name: icalperiodtype_is_null_period
functions.description: Returns true if the period is a null period.
requirements: p should be a valid icalperiodtype struct

functions.name: icalperiodtype_is_valid_period
functions.description: Returns true if the period is a valid period (non-null and structurally consistent).
requirements: Pass a valid icalperiodtype; null periods are not valid

functions.name: icalenum_reqstat_desc
functions.description: Returns descriptive text for a request status code.
requirements: stat must be a valid icalrequeststatus enum
Returned string is library-owned; do not free

functions.name: icalenum_reqstat_major
functions.description: Returns the major number of a request status code.
requirements: stat must be a valid icalrequeststatus enum

functions.name: icalenum_reqstat_minor
functions.description: Returns the minor number of a request status code.
requirements: stat must be a valid icalrequeststatus enum

functions.name: icalenum_num_to_reqstat
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT icalrequeststatus icalenum_num_to_reqstat(short major, short minor);
functions.description: Builds an icalrequeststatus enum from major/minor numeric parts.
requirements: major/minor should be valid parts as per libical definitions

functions.name: icalenum_reqstat_code
functions.description: Returns the numeric status code string for a request status. Returned string is library-owned.
requirements: stat must be a valid icalrequeststatus enum
Do not free returned string

functions.name: icalenum_reqstat_code_r
functions.description: Returns the numeric status code string for a request status. Returned string is library-owned (per header note).
requirements: stat must be a valid icalrequeststatus enum
Do not free returned string

functions.name: icaltriggertype_from_seconds
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT struct icaltriggertype icaltriggertype_from_seconds(const int reltime);
functions.description: Constructs a trigger type from a relative time in seconds (duration).
requirements: reltime is a signed number of seconds relative to an event time

functions.name: icaltriggertype_from_string
functions.description: Parses a trigger from string form into an icaltriggertype.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL string in accepted trigger format

functions.name: icaltriggertype_is_null_trigger
functions.description: Returns true if the trigger is a null/empty trigger.
requirements: tr must be a valid struct

functions.name: icaltriggertype_is_bad_trigger
functions.description: Returns true if the trigger represents a bad/error trigger.
requirements: Use for validating parsed trigger objects

functions.name: icalreqstattype_from_string
functions.description: Parses a REQUEST-STATUS value into an icalreqstattype. The desc string is library-static; debug string is owned by icalvalue and not to be freed manually.
requirements: str must be non-NULL and formatted per RFC
Returned struct is by value; do not free desc/debug pointers

functions.name: icalreqstattype_as_string
functions.description: Formats an icalreqstattype as a string. Returned pointer is library-owned.
requirements: Do not free returned pointer

functions.name: icalreqstattype_as_string_r
functions.description: Formats an icalreqstattype as a caller-owned string.
requirements: Caller must free returned string with appropriate function

functions.name: ical_get_unknown_token_handling_setting
functions.description: Gets current library setting for handling unknown tokens (parameters, possibly props/components).
requirements: None

functions.name: ical_set_unknown_token_handling_setting
functions.description: Sets how the library handles unknown tokens (assume IANA, discard, or treat as error).
requirements: newSetting must be one of ICAL_ASSUME_IANA_TOKEN, ICAL_DISCARD_TOKEN, ICAL_TREAT_AS_ERROR

functions.name: icalarray_new
functions.description: Creates a dynamically growing array container for fixed-size elements.
requirements: element_size must be >= 1; using an invalid value leads to undefined behavior
On allocation failure returns NULL and sets icalerrno=ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR
Caller owns returned array; free with icalarray_free()

functions.name: icalarray_copy
functions.description: Deep-copies an icalarray and its elements (by value) including metadata.
requirements: If array is NULL, returns NULL
On allocation error sets icalerrno=ICAL_ALLOCATION_ERROR
Caller must free result with icalarray_free()

functions.name: icalarray_free
functions.description: Frees an icalarray and its storage.
requirements: array may be NULL; after call pointer is invalid

functions.name: icalarray_append
functions.description: Appends an element to the end of the array, reallocating as necessary.
requirements: array must not be NULL
element must not be NULL and must point to at least element_size bytes
Element is copied; caller retains ownership of input buffer

functions.name: icalarray_remove_element_at
functions.description: Removes the element at the given index. If position is out-of-range, removes the last element.
requirements: array must not be NULL
Array must not be empty when removing; otherwise undefined behavior

functions.name: icalarray_element_at
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the element at the given index within the array’s internal storage.
requirements: array must not be NULL
position must be a valid index; otherwise undefined behavior
Returned pointer is owned by the array; do not free

functions.name: icalarray_set_element_at
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT void icalarray_set_element_at(icalarray *array, const void *element, size_t position);
functions.description: Overwrites the element at the given index with the provided value (by copy).
requirements: array and element must not be NULL
position must be within existing element range; otherwise undefined behavior
Caller must free any heap data referenced by the previous element if needed

functions.name: icalarray_sort
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT void icalarray_sort(icalarray *array,                                         int (*compare)(const void *, const void *));
functions.description: Sorts array elements using the provided comparator (qsort-like).
requirements: array and compare must not be NULL

functions.name: icalenumarray_element_at
functions.description: Returns the enumarray element at the given slot, or NULL if not set.
requirements: array may be NULL; returns NULL
position must be within slots set; else NULL

functions.name: icalenumarray_size
functions.description: Returns the count of elements in the enum array.
requirements: If array is NULL, returns 0

functions.name: icalenumarray_find
functions.description: Finds the first occurrence of an element (matching val and xvalue bytes) and returns its position; if not found returns array size.
requirements: If array or needle is NULL, behaves as not-found (returns size)

functions.name: icalenumarray_append
functions.description: Appends an element without duplicate checking.
requirements: If array or elem is NULL, no operation is performed

functions.name: icalenumarray_add
functions.description: Adds an element unless a byte-equal element already exists.
requirements: If array or elem is NULL, no operation is performed

functions.name: icalenumarray_remove_element_at
functions.description: Removes the element at the given position if within range.
requirements: If array is NULL or position >= count, no operation

functions.name: icalenumarray_remove
functions.description: Removes all occurrences of a given element (matching val and xvalue).
requirements: If array or del is NULL, no operation

functions.name: icalenumarray_free
functions.description: Frees the enumarray and its elements.
requirements: If array is NULL, no operation

functions.name: icalenumarray_sort
functions.description: Sorts enumarray elements in ascending byte order.
requirements: If array is NULL, no operation

functions.name: icalenumarray_clone
functions.description: Creates an independent clone of the enumarray and its elements.
requirements: If array is NULL, returns NULL
Caller must free the clone with icalenumarray_free()

functions.name: icalstrarray_element_at
functions.description: Returns the string at the given slot, or NULL if not set.
requirements: If array is NULL, returns NULL
Returned string is owned by the array; do not free

functions.name: icalstrarray_size
functions.description: Returns the count of strings in the array.
requirements: If array is NULL, returns 0

functions.name: icalstrarray_find
functions.description: Finds the first occurrence of a byte-equal string and returns its position or the array size if not found.
requirements: If array or needle is NULL, behaves as not-found (returns size)

functions.name: icalstrarray_append
functions.description: Appends a string to the array without duplicate checking.
requirements: If array or elem is NULL, no operation
Array stores the string pointer (per icalarray semantics for char* slots, caller should consider element lifetime)

functions.name: icalstrarray_add
functions.description: Adds a string to the array unless an equal string already exists.

functions.name: icalarray_new
functions.description: Creates a new dynamically-growing array that stores fixed-size elements. element_size specifies the size in bytes of each element; increment_size controls growth granularity (0 selects a library default). Returns a new icalarray on success or NULL on allocation failure (icalerrno set to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR). Typical usage: construct, append elements via icalarray_append, access with icalarray_element_at, then free with icalarray_free.
requirements: element_size must be >= 1; otherwise using the returned object results in undefined behavior.
increment_size may be 0 to use the library default growth increment.
On failure, the function returns NULL; the caller should check for NULL and may inspect icalerrno (set to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR).
The returned icalarray is owned by the caller and must be freed with icalarray_free().

functions.name: icalarray_copy
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of an existing icalarray, duplicating its properties and elements. Returns a new icalarray that the caller owns, or NULL if input is NULL or if allocation fails (icalerrno set to ICAL_ALLOCATION_ERROR on allocation failure).
requirements: array may be NULL; if NULL, the function returns NULL.
On allocation failure, the function returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_ALLOCATION_ERROR; callers should check for NULL.
The returned icalarray must be freed with icalarray_free() by the caller.

functions.name: icalarray_free
functions.description: Frees an icalarray and all storage it owns. After this call, the array pointer must not be used. Intended to release arrays created by icalarray_new or icalarray_copy.
requirements: array must be a valid icalarray previously allocated by libical (e.g., via icalarray_new or icalarray_copy).
After calling, the array and any pointers obtained via icalarray_element_at become invalid and must not be used.
Whether passing NULL is allowed is not specified; behavior for array == NULL is unknown.

functions.name: icalarray_append
functions.description: Appends a new element to the end of the array, growing internal storage as needed. The element data is copied into the array using the array’s element_size.
requirements: array must be non-NULL; otherwise behavior is undefined.
element must be non-NULL; otherwise behavior is undefined.
element must point to at least element_size bytes of readable memory compatible with the array’s element size.
The function copies the element; the caller retains ownership of the source buffer.

functions.name: icalarray_remove_element_at
functions.description: Removes the element at the specified position. If position does not exist (is out of range), the last element is removed. The function compacts the array after removal.
requirements: array must be non-NULL; otherwise behavior is undefined.
The array must not be empty; removing from an empty array results in undefined behavior.
If position is out of range, the function removes the last element (documented behavior).

functions.name: icalarray_element_at
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the element stored at position within the array. The returned pointer refers to the element inside the array storage; callers may read and write the element in place. Do not free the returned pointer.
requirements: array must be non-NULL; otherwise behavior is undefined.
position must be a valid index within the array; otherwise behavior is undefined.
The returned pointer is owned by the array; the caller must not free it and must not use it after the array is freed.
Modifying the pointed-to memory updates the element in the array.

functions.name: icalarray_set_element_at
functions.signature: void icalarray_set_element_at(icalarray *array, const void *element, size_t position);
functions.description: Overwrites the element at position with the provided value, copying element_size bytes from element into the array. Intended for replacing existing entries without changing array length.
requirements: array must be non-NULL; otherwise behavior is undefined.
element must be non-NULL; otherwise behavior is undefined.
position must refer to an existing element (must not be greater than the last valid index); otherwise behavior is undefined.
element must point to at least element_size bytes of readable memory compatible with the array’s element size.
Overwriting does not manage resources of the old element; callers are responsible for freeing any heap-allocated data held by the element being overwritten.

functions.name: icalarray_sort
functions.signature: void icalarray_sort(icalarray *array, int (*compare)(const void *, const void *));
functions.description: Sorts the array in-place using the provided comparator. The comparator receives pointers to elements as stored in the array (each element_size bytes) and must return negative/zero/positive like qsort-style comparisons.
requirements: array must be non-NULL; otherwise behavior is undefined.
compare must be non-NULL; otherwise behavior is undefined.
The compare function must accept pointers to the array’s element type and implement a strict weak ordering consistent with the stored data.
The compare callback must not assume NUL-termination or other layout beyond element_size bytes; it must cast appropriately.

functions.name: icalattach_new_from_url
functions.description: Create a new reference-counted icalattach that represents an ATTACH value backed by a URL. Use when you want the attachment to refer to an external resource. On success returns a new icalattach; caller owns a reference and must later release it with icalattach_unref(). On failure returns NULL and sets error indicators.
requirements: url must not be NULL; if NULL, the function returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect errors; on allocation failure errno may be set to ENOMEM.
The returned icalattach is reference-counted; the caller must call icalattach_unref() when done.
After unref reduces the last reference, the object is destroyed and must not be used.

functions.name: icalattach_new_from_data
functions.description: Create a new reference-counted icalattach that represents an ATTACH value backed by in-memory data. Typically used for embedded/binary data attachments. Returns a new icalattach on success; caller owns a reference and must later release it with icalattach_unref(). Note: the free function pointer type is defined, but documentation states it is currently not used by libical.
requirements: data must not be NULL; if NULL, the function returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR. (Header comment mistakenly mentions url; the intended parameter is data.)
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect errors; on allocation failure errno may be set to ENOMEM.

Do not assume free_fn will be invoked by the library; manage the lifetime of the memory referenced by data accordingly so that accesses via icalattach_get_data() remain valid while the icalattach is in use.
The returned icalattach is reference-counted; the caller must call icalattach_unref() when done.
After unref reduces the last reference, the object is destroyed and must not be used.

functions.name: icalattach_ref
functions.description: Increment the reference count of an icalattach to indicate an additional owner. Use when sharing an icalattach across components or threads that maintain separate lifetimes. Must be paired with a later icalattach_unref() for the same reference.
requirements: attach must not be NULL; if NULL, the function sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
The internal reference count must not be negative; if it is, the function sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
Each successful call to icalattach_ref() must be matched by a corresponding icalattach_unref() by the same logical owner.

functions.name: icalattach_unref
functions.description: Decrement the reference count of an icalattach. When the count reaches zero, the object is freed. After the final unref, the pointer must not be used.
requirements: attach must not be NULL; if NULL, the function sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
Do not call unref more times than the number of owned references; the internal reference count must not become negative (otherwise icalerrno is set to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR).
After this call, if it was the last reference, the object is destroyed and must not be accessed.

functions.name: icaldurationtype_from_seconds
functions.description: Constructs an icaldurationtype from a signed number of seconds. If seconds is negative, the resulting struct has is_neg set and the seconds field is stored as a positive magnitude; values are not refactored into minutes/hours/days.
requirements: seconds may be any int (negative values indicate a duration pointing backward in time).
The resulting structure’s seconds field is a positive magnitude; is_neg indicates sign (callers should not expect normalization into minutes/hours/days).

functions.name: icaldurationtype_from_string
functions.description: Parses an iCal-formatted duration string (e.g., PnW, PnDTnHnMnS, optional leading +/−) into an icaldurationtype. On malformed input, sets icalerrno to ICAL_MALFORMEDDATA_ERROR and returns a bad duration.
requirements: str should be an iCal duration string (e.g., "+PT05M", "-P2DT3H").
On error, the function returns a bad duration; callers should check with icaldurationtype_is_bad_duration() and/or inspect icalerrno for ICAL_MALFORMEDDATA_ERROR.

functions.name: icaldurationtype_as_seconds
functions.description: Returns the signed number of seconds represented by an icaldurationtype. Only the hours/minutes/seconds fields (with is_neg) are converted; non-zero days or weeks in the struct are considered an error condition.
requirements: duration should not contain non-zero days or weeks; only hours, minutes, and seconds are supported for conversion.
The returned value may be negative if duration.is_neg is set.

functions.name: icaldurationtype_as_ical_string
functions.description: Formats an icaldurationtype as an iCal-compliant duration string and returns a newly allocated C string.
requirements: The returned string is owned by the caller and must be freed with icalmemory_free_buffer() when no longer needed.

functions.name: icaldurationtype_as_ical_string_r
functions.description: Formats an icaldurationtype as an iCal-compliant duration string and returns a pointer to memory owned by libical.
requirements: The returned string is owned by libical; the caller must not free it.

functions.name: icaldurationtype_null_duration
functions.description: Returns an icaldurationtype representing a zero-length duration (all fields zero, non-negative). Useful for initialization and comparisons.

functions.name: icaldurationtype_bad_duration
functions.description: Returns a sentinel icaldurationtype indicating an invalid or error state. Typically used as a return value on parse or conversion failure.

functions.name: icaldurationtype_is_null_duration
functions.description: Checks whether a duration is the zero-length (null) duration.

functions.name: icaldurationtype_is_bad_duration
functions.description: Checks whether a duration is the special bad/invalid duration sentinel.

functions.name: icalduration_extend
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT struct icaltimetype icalduration_extend(struct icaltimetype t, struct icaldurationtype d);
functions.description: Returns a new icaltimetype equal to t extended by (added with) duration d. Negative durations subtract time.
requirements: t should be a valid/initialized icaltimetype.
d should be a valid/initialized icaldurationtype.

functions.name: icalduration_from_times
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT struct icaldurationtype icalduration_from_times(struct icaltimetype t1, struct icaltimetype t2);
functions.description: Computes the duration between two icaltimetype values t1 and t2, returning an icaldurationtype representing the elapsed time from t1 to t2.
requirements: t1 and t2 should be valid/initialized icaltimetype values.

functions.name: icalenumarray_new
functions.signature: icalenumarray *icalenumarray_new(size_t increment_size) /* macro wrapper over icalarray_new(sizeof(icalenumarray_element), increment_size) */
functions.description: Creates a new icalenumarray (an icalarray specialized for icalenumarray_element). This is defined as a macro that forwards to icalarray_new with element size sizeof(icalenumarray_element). Use when you need a dynamic array of {int val; const char *xvalue;}. Returns a heap-allocated array owned by the caller; free with icalenumarray_free() when done. On allocation failure it returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR.
requirements: May be called with increment_size == 0 to select the library’s default growth increment.
On failure, the function-like macro returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR; callers must check for NULL before use.
The returned array is owned by the caller and must be released with icalenumarray_free().

functions.name: icalenumarray_element_at
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the element stored at the given position in the array. Use to read an existing item without copying. The returned pointer is to internal storage and must not be freed or modified by the caller.
requirements: array must be non-NULL; otherwise returns NULL.
position must refer to a set element (position < icalenumarray_size(array)); otherwise returns NULL.
The returned pointer is owned by the array; do not free it or store it beyond the lifetime of array.

functions.name: icalenumarray_size
functions.description: Returns the count of elements currently stored in the array. Use to bounds-check positions or iterate.
requirements: If array is NULL, the return value is 0.

functions.name: icalenumarray_find
functions.description: Searches the array for the first occurrence of an element equal to needle (numeric val equal and xvalue byte-equal, with xvalue comparison treating the optional pointer as a byte string). Returns the position if found; otherwise returns icalenumarray_size(array).
requirements: If array is NULL or needle is NULL, the function returns icalenumarray_size(array) (or 0 if array is NULL), i.e., the not-found sentinel.
Equality semantics: numeric val must match and xvalue pointers must compare byte-equal; NULL xvalue is allowed per documentation’s “optional xvalue”.
Callers must treat a return equal to icalenumarray_size(array) as ‘not found’.
array must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: icalenumarray_append
functions.description: Appends elem to the end of the array without checking for duplicates. Use when duplicates are acceptable or intended.
requirements: If array is NULL or elem is NULL, this function does nothing (noop).

The element’s contents are stored into the array; ownership of elem itself remains with the caller. Any pointer fields within the element (xvalue) are stored as provided; lifetime/ownership of xvalue is not specified in this header (unknown).
Callers should not assume duplicate suppression; use icalenumarray_add() instead if needed.

functions.name: icalenumarray_add
functions.description: Appends elem to the array unless a byte-equal string is already present in the array. Intended to avoid duplicates according to the library’s duplicate criterion.
requirements: If array is NULL or elem is NULL, this function does nothing (noop).
Duplicate check behavior is defined as omitting an append when a byte-equal string is already present in the array; finer details beyond this phrasing are not specified here (unknown).
If precise duplicate semantics are required (e.g., also matching numeric val), consult implementation; from header comments, find() uses val and xvalue, but add() only states byte-equal string check.

functions.name: icalenumarray_remove_element_at
functions.description: Removes the element at the specified position from the array. Elements after the removed one may shift to fill the gap.
requirements: If array is NULL, this is a noop.
If position is greater than or equal to icalenumarray_size(array), this is a noop.

functions.name: icalenumarray_remove
functions.description: Removes all occurrences of the specified element from the array. Matching is based on the library’s equality for elements (numeric val equal and xvalue byte-equal, per find’s description).
requirements: If array is NULL or del is NULL, this is a noop.

functions.name: icalenumarray_free
functions.description: Frees the array and all its elements’ storage. Call when the array is no longer needed.
requirements: If array is NULL, this is a noop.
After calling, any pointers previously obtained via icalenumarray_element_at() become invalid.
Caller must not use array after freeing it.

functions.name: icalenumarray_sort
functions.description: Sorts the array in ascending order, comparing elements as bytes. Use to normalize ordering before comparisons or serialization.
requirements: If array is NULL, this is a noop.
Sorting order is byte-wise ascending per element representation; exact comparator details beyond this are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: icalenumarray_clone
functions.description: Creates an independent copy of the array and all its elements. Use when you need to mutate a copy without affecting the original.
requirements: If array is NULL, returns NULL; callers must check the return value before use.
The returned array is owned by the caller and must be freed with icalenumarray_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: icalenum_reqstat_desc
functions.description: Returns a human‑readable, descriptive text for the given request status code. Use this to present a textual explanation of an icalrequeststatus value.
requirements: stat must be a valid icalrequeststatus enumerator.

functions.name: icalenum_reqstat_major
functions.description: Returns the major (first) numeric component of the given request status code. Intended for extracting the high‑level class of a status.
requirements: stat must be a valid icalrequeststatus enumerator.

functions.name: icalenum_reqstat_minor
functions.description: Returns the minor (second) numeric component of the given request status code. Intended for extracting the sub‑class/detail of a status.
requirements: stat must be a valid icalrequeststatus enumerator.

functions.name: icalenum_num_to_reqstat
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT icalrequeststatus icalenum_num_to_reqstat(short major, short minor);
functions.description: Maps a pair of numeric major/minor values to the corresponding icalrequeststatus enumerator.
requirements: major and minor should correspond to a defined request status pair; behavior is unknown if the pair does not map to a defined icalrequeststatus (result may be ICAL_UNKNOWN_STATUS or another sentinel; not specified in this header).

functions.name: icalenum_reqstat_code
functions.description: Returns the standardized code string for a request status (e.g., the numeric "major.minor" form) for the given icalrequeststatus. Use when you need the canonical code value rather than descriptive text. Ownership and mutability of the returned string are not specified here.
requirements: stat must be a valid icalrequeststatus enumerator.
Memory ownership, lifetime, and thread‑safety characteristics of the returned char* are unknown based on this header; callers should not assume mutability or that it persists beyond immediate use.

functions.name: icalenum_reqstat_code_r
functions.description: Returns the code string for a request status, analogous to icalenum_reqstat_code. The suffix "_r" typically indicates a reentrant/thread‑safe variant in this library, but the exact ownership and lifetime of the returned pointer are not specified by this header.
requirements: stat must be a valid icalrequeststatus enumerator.
Specifics about allocation, ownership, and whether the returned char* must be freed by the caller are unknown from this header; treat usage conservatively and consult implementation/docs.

functions.name: icalerror_stop_here
functions.description: Debug hook invoked just before an error is triggered. Primarily intended for setting a debugger breakpoint to inspect state when libical reports an error. It performs no state change itself.
requirements: May be called at any time; has no arguments and no return value.
Intended for debugging; calling it in production has no defined side effects other than being a hook.

functions.name: icalerror_crash_here
functions.description: Hook that intentionally aborts the process in the case of an error. Used by libical when a fatal error policy is in effect.
requirements: Calling this function will abort the process; only call when it is acceptable to terminate immediately.

functions.name: icalerrno_return
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current global libical error variable (icalerrno). The pointer can be used to read or write the current error code.
requirements: The returned pointer refers to library-owned storage; do not free it.
The pointed-to value may be modified by libical calls; callers should not assume thread-safety unless otherwise synchronized (thread-safety not specified).

functions.name: icalerror_set_errors_are_fatal
functions.description: Controls whether libical treats errors as fatal. When set to true, certain error-setting operations will print a warning and abort the process.
requirements: Not thread safe; avoid changing this setting in multithreaded programs or protect with external synchronization.
Pass true to enable fatal behavior, false to disable.

functions.name: icalerror_get_errors_are_fatal
functions.description: Queries whether libical is currently configured to treat errors as fatal.
requirements: None.

functions.name: icalerror_clear_errno
functions.description: Resets the global error code (icalerrno) to ICAL_NO_ERROR.
requirements: None.

functions.name: icalerror_strerror
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description string for the specified libical error code. If the code is not recognized, returns the description for ICAL_UNKNOWN_ERROR. The returned string is library-owned.
requirements: Argument e should be a valid icalerrorenum value; unknown values are handled by returning the ICAL_UNKNOWN_ERROR description.
Returned C string is library-owned; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: icalerror_perror
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description string for the current global error (icalerrno). If the error is not recognized, returns the description for ICAL_UNKNOWN_ERROR. The returned string is library-owned.
requirements: Returned C string is library-owned; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: ical_bt
functions.description: Prints a backtrace when supported (built with HAVE_BACKTRACE). Useful for debugging after an error has been set.
requirements: Functionality depends on platform/build support (HAVE_BACKTRACE); on unsupported systems it may do nothing.

functions.name: icalerror_set_error_state
functions.description: Sets the severity (error state) for a given error type, e.g., make ICAL_PARSE_ERROR non-fatal.
requirements: Argument error should be a valid icalerrorenum.
Argument state must be one of ICAL_ERROR_FATAL, ICAL_ERROR_NONFATAL, or ICAL_ERROR_DEFAULT.

functions.name: icalerror_get_error_state
functions.description: Returns the current severity (error state) for the given error type. For unknown error types, the state ICAL_ERROR_UNKNOWN may be returned.
requirements: Argument error should be a valid icalerrorenum; otherwise expect ICAL_ERROR_UNKNOWN.

functions.name: icalerror_error_from_string
functions.description: Parses an error name string and returns the corresponding icalerrorenum value. If the name is not recognized, returns ICAL_UNKNOWN_ERROR.
requirements: str must be a null-terminated C string naming an error (e.g., "PARSE", "INTERNAL").
Returns ICAL_UNKNOWN_ERROR if the string does not map to a known error.

functions.name: icalerror_set_errno
functions.description: Sets the global error (icalerrno) to the given code. If the error’s configured state is fatal, or the state is DEFAULT and errors-are-fatal is enabled, this prints a warning to stderr and aborts the process.
requirements: Argument x should be a valid icalerrorenum.
Callers must be prepared for process termination when the error is configured as fatal or default with fatal mode enabled.

functions.name: icalerror_supress
functions.description: Suppresses (marks as ICAL_ERROR_NONFATAL) the specified error by name and returns its previous severity state. Can be reverted with icalerror_restore(). Note: function name is spelled "supress" (one 'p').
requirements: error must be a null-terminated C string naming an error type recognizable by the library (same naming used by icalerror_error_from_string).
Returns the previous severity state of the named error.

functions.name: icalerror_restore
functions.description: Assigns the given error (by name) the provided severity (error state), typically to restore a previously suppressed error to its original state.
requirements: error must be a null-terminated C string naming an error type recognizable by the library.
es must be a valid icalerrorstate (e.g., ICAL_ERROR_DEFAULT to restore default behavior).

functions.name: icallangbind_new_array
functions.description: Allocates a new contiguous array of int elements intended for language bindings and returns a pointer to the first element. The array length is the requested size. Use icallangbind_free_array to release it. Returns NULL on allocation failure (inferred).
requirements: size must be the intended number of elements to allocate; behavior for size == 0 is unspecified (inferred from typical C allocation semantics).
The returned pointer must be freed with icallangbind_free_array; do not free it with other deallocators (inferred from pairing with the free function).
Check for a NULL return before use to handle allocation failure (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_free_array
functions.description: Frees an int array previously allocated by icallangbind_new_array. After this call, the pointer must not be used.
requirements: array must be a pointer previously returned by icallangbind_new_array or NULL (NULL is typically a no-op in C; exact behavior not documented).
Do not pass the same pointer more than once; double-free is undefined behavior (inferred).
Do not use the pointer after freeing it (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_access_array
functions.description: Returns the value stored at the specified index of an int array created by icallangbind_new_array. Intended to provide bounds-safe access for language bindings; however, the header does not specify bounds checking or error signaling.
requirements: array must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid int array (ideally one created by icallangbind_new_array).
index must refer to a valid element within the allocated array (0 <= index < size); behavior for out-of-range indices is unspecified/undefined (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_get_first_property
functions.description: Initializes an iteration over the properties of the given icalcomponent and returns the first icalproperty that matches the specified property name. Use icallangbind_get_next_property to continue iteration. The property name is provided as a string for language bindings (e.g., "DTSTART"). Returns NULL if none is found or on invalid input (inferred).
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized icalcomponent pointer.
prop must point to a NUL-terminated property name string recognized by libical (e.g., an iCalendar property like "DTSTART"); exact accepted values and case-sensitivity are not documented here.
Call this function before calling icallangbind_get_next_property for a given iteration sequence (inferred).
Do not modify the component’s property list between calls to first/next for the same iteration (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_get_next_property
functions.description: Continues an iteration started by icallangbind_get_first_property over properties of the given icalcomponent that match the specified property name, returning the next matching icalproperty. Returns NULL when no more matches are available (inferred).
requirements: Must be preceded by a successful call to icallangbind_get_first_property with the same component and the same prop value (inferred).
c must be a valid, initialized icalcomponent pointer.
prop must be the same property name used to start the iteration; mixing names mid-iteration is unspecified (inferred).
Do not modify the component’s property list during iteration (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_get_first_component
functions.description: Initializes an iteration over child components of the given icalcomponent and returns the first icalcomponent that matches the specified component name (e.g., "VEVENT"). Use icallangbind_get_next_component to continue. Returns NULL if none is found (inferred).
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized icalcomponent pointer.
comp must point to a NUL-terminated component name string recognized by libical (e.g., "VEVENT", "VTODO"); exact accepted values and case-sensitivity are not documented here.
Call this function before calling icallangbind_get_next_component for a given iteration sequence (inferred).
Do not modify the component’s child list between calls to first/next for the same iteration (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_get_next_component
functions.description: Continues an iteration started by icallangbind_get_first_component over child components of a given type, returning the next matching icalcomponent. Returns NULL when the iteration is exhausted (inferred).
requirements: Must be preceded by a successful call to icallangbind_get_first_component with the same component and the same comp value (inferred).
c must be a valid, initialized icalcomponent pointer.
comp should be the same component name used to start the iteration; mixing names mid-iteration is unspecified (inferred).
Do not modify the component’s child list during iteration (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_get_first_parameter
functions.description: Initializes an iteration over the parameters of the given icalproperty and returns the first icalparameter. Use icallangbind_get_next_parameter to continue. Returns NULL if no parameters exist (inferred).
requirements: prop must be a valid, initialized icalproperty pointer.
Call this function before calling icallangbind_get_next_parameter for a given iteration sequence (inferred).
Do not modify the property’s parameters between calls to first/next for the same iteration (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_get_next_parameter
functions.description: Continues an iteration started by icallangbind_get_first_parameter over parameters of the given icalproperty, returning the next icalparameter. Returns NULL when there are no more (inferred).
requirements: Must be preceded by a successful call to icallangbind_get_first_parameter with the same property (inferred).
prop must be a valid, initialized icalproperty pointer.
Do not modify the property’s parameters during iteration (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_property_eval_string
functions.description: Returns a textual representation of an icalproperty’s value (and possibly associated data) as a single string, using sep as a separator when needed. Intended for language bindings. The returned pointer is a non-owning const char* that likely refers to an internal static buffer that may be overwritten by subsequent calls and is not thread-safe (inferred from naming and presence of the _r variant). Returns NULL on error (inferred).
requirements: prop must be a valid, initialized icalproperty pointer.
sep must be a pointer to a NUL-terminated C string; behavior for NULL is unspecified in this header.
Do not assume the returned pointer remains valid after subsequent libical calls; copy it if persistence is required (inferred).
Do not attempt to free the returned pointer (const, non-owning) (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_property_eval_string_r
functions.description: Reentrant/allocating variant of icallangbind_property_eval_string. Produces and returns a newly allocated C string containing a textual representation of the property, using sep as a separator. The caller owns the returned buffer and must free it using the appropriate deallocator (exact function not specified in this header; typically free() or a libical-specific free) (inferred). Returns NULL on error (inferred).
requirements: prop must be a valid, initialized icalproperty pointer.
sep must be a pointer to a NUL-terminated C string; behavior for NULL is unspecified in this header.
Caller must release the returned buffer; the exact required deallocator is not specified here—consult libical’s memory management documentation (inferred).
Always check for a NULL return before use (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_string_to_open_flag
functions.description: Converts a text description of open mode or flags into an integer bitmask used by libical file or storage APIs. Common inputs likely include strings such as "r", "w", or similar (exact accepted values not documented here). Returns an integer flag value; error signaling is not specified in this header (inferred).
requirements: str must be a pointer to a NUL-terminated C string representing the desired open mode/flags; the set of valid values is not specified here.
Caller should validate the return value against expected flags or check for library-documented error values (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_quote_as_ical
functions.description: Returns an iCalendar-escaped version of the input string (e.g., escaping commas, semicolons, and backslashes) suitable for inclusion in .ics text. The returned pointer is a non-owning const char* that likely refers to an internal static buffer that can be overwritten by subsequent calls and is not thread-safe (inferred from naming and presence of the _r variant). Returns NULL on error (inferred).
requirements: str must be a pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.
Do not free the returned pointer (const, non-owning) (inferred).
Copy the returned data if it must persist across subsequent calls or across threads (inferred).

functions.name: icallangbind_quote_as_ical_r
