functions.description: Reentrant/allocating variant of icallangbind_quote_as_ical. Returns a newly allocated C string containing the iCalendar-escaped form of the input. The caller owns the buffer and must free it with the appropriate deallocator (exact function not specified in this header; typically free() or a libical-specific free) (inferred). Returns NULL on error (inferred).
requirements: str must be a pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.
Caller must release the returned buffer; the exact required deallocator is not specified here—consult libical’s memory management documentation (inferred).
Always check for a NULL return before use (inferred).

functions.name: icalmemory_tmp_buffer
functions.description: Allocates a zeroed temporary buffer on libical’s per-thread ring buffer and returns it. The memory is owned by libical and will be reclaimed automatically as the ring advances. Use this when you need short-lived scratch space without manual free.
requirements: Caller must not free the returned pointer; ownership remains with libical and it may be reclaimed automatically.
Do not assume the buffer is exactly size bytes; it will be at least MIN_BUFFER_SIZE and zero-initialized.
On allocation failure, function returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR; caller should check for NULL before use.
Temporary buffers must not be passed to functions that reallocate (e.g., icalmemory_resize_buffer, icalmemory_append_*).

functions.name: icalmemory_tmp_copy
functions.description: Creates a temporary copy of the given C string on the libical ring buffer and returns it. The memory is owned by libical and reclaimed automatically.
requirements: str must not be NULL; the function calls strlen(str) and passing NULL may segfault.
Caller must not free the returned pointer; it is reclaimed automatically as the ring advances.
Returned data is temporary; do not store beyond the lifetime of the ring slot and do not pass to APIs that may free/realloc it.

functions.name: icalmemory_add_tmp_buffer
functions.description: Adds an externally allocated buffer to the ring so libical will free it automatically later via icalmemory_free_buffer(). Use to hand ownership of a compatible allocation to the ring.
requirements: buf may be NULL (no error).
After calling, ownership transfers to libical; caller must not free buf to avoid double free.
buf must have been allocated in a manner compatible with the currently configured icalmemory_free_buffer() (i.e., with the allocator set via icalmemory_set_mem_alloc_funcs or standard malloc family).

functions.name: icalmemory_free_ring
functions.description: Frees all memory currently managed by the ring buffer for the calling thread. In threaded or thread-local builds, each thread has its own ring; call this in each thread to release its ring.
requirements: In multi-threaded/thread-local configurations, call once per thread to free all rings if global cleanup is required.
Only frees ring-managed temporary buffers; does not affect caller-owned buffers created with icalmemory_new_buffer/resize/strdup.

functions.name: icalmemory_set_mem_alloc_funcs
functions.signature: void icalmemory_set_mem_alloc_funcs(icalmemory_malloc_f f_malloc, icalmemory_realloc_f f_realloc, icalmemory_free_f f_free)
functions.description: Configures custom allocation, reallocation, and free functions used by libical core for memory management instead of the C library defaults. Affects core libical components (not libicalvcal).
requirements: Function pointers should implement malloc/realloc/free semantics compatible with how libical uses them (inferred from purpose).
Call before operations that should use the custom functions to ensure consistent allocation/freeing.
Only core libical uses these hooks; other components like libicalvcal are not affected.

functions.name: icalmemory_get_mem_alloc_funcs
functions.description: Retrieves the current allocation, reallocation, and free function pointers used by libical core.
requirements: If you need a particular pointer, pass a non-NULL output parameter for it; unspecified behavior if any output pointer is NULL (not documented).
Values returned reflect core libical settings; other components like libicalvcal may differ.

functions.name: icalmemory_new_buffer
functions.description: Allocates a new zero-initialized caller-owned buffer of the given size using the currently configured allocator. Must be freed with icalmemory_free_buffer().
requirements: On allocation failure, returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR; caller must check for NULL.
Caller owns the returned memory and must release it with icalmemory_free_buffer().
Buffer is zeroed on allocation.

functions.name: icalmemory_resize_buffer
functions.description: Reallocates a caller-owned buffer (originally from icalmemory_new_buffer or compatible allocator) to the new size using the configured reallocator. Returns the new buffer pointer; the old pointer must not be used after a successful call.
requirements: Must not be used on temporary (ring) buffers; only use with buffers allocated via icalmemory_new_buffer (or otherwise compatible with the configured allocator).
On reallocation failure, returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR; caller must handle NULL and consider the original buffer content per realloc semantics.
If successful, the old buf pointer becomes invalid; always use the returned pointer.
buf should be a valid pointer previously allocated with the compatible allocator.

functions.name: icalmemory_free_buffer
functions.description: Frees a caller-owned buffer using the currently configured deallocator. Intended for buffers created by icalmemory_new_buffer, icalmemory_resize_buffer, or icalmemory_strdup.
requirements: buf must be a pointer allocated with the compatible allocator (default malloc family or as set via icalmemory_set_mem_alloc_funcs).
Do not pass temporary (ring) buffers; those are freed automatically by the ring.
Safe behavior for NULL is not documented; callers should avoid passing NULL unless implementation guarantees it.

functions.name: icalmemory_append_string
functions.signature: void icalmemory_append_string(char **buf, char **pos, size_t *buf_size, const char *string)
functions.description: Appends a NUL-terminated string to a caller-owned buffer at the position pointer, growing the buffer with the configured reallocator if needed. Updates buf (if reallocated), pos to the last written byte (typically '\0'), and buf_size to the new size.
requirements: Must not be used with temporary (ring) buffers; only with caller-owned buffers (e.g., from icalmemory_new_buffer).
buf, *buf, pos, *pos, buf_size, and string must all be non-NULL; otherwise sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR (no behavior guaranteed).
*pos must point within *buf at the intended append position; function writes starting at *pos and maintains a terminating '\0'.
Caller must honor updated pointers after the call (buf may be reallocated; pos and buf_size may change).

functions.name: icalmemory_append_char
functions.signature: void icalmemory_append_char(char **buf, char **pos, size_t *buf_size, char ch)
functions.description: Appends a single character plus a terminating '\0' to a caller-owned buffer at the position pointer, reallocating the buffer if necessary. Updates buf (if reallocated), pos to the new terminator, and buf_size.
requirements: Must not be used with temporary (ring) buffers; only with caller-owned buffers (e.g., from icalmemory_new_buffer).
buf, *buf, pos, *pos, and buf_size must all be non-NULL; otherwise sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
*pos must point within *buf at the intended append position; function writes ch and then a '\0'.
Caller must use the possibly updated pointers after the call.

functions.name: icalmemory_strdup
functions.description: Duplicates a C string using icalmemory_new_buffer for allocation and returns a caller-owned copy. Use instead of strdup() to ensure compatibility with libical’s memory hooks. Free with icalmemory_free_buffer().
requirements: s must not be NULL; passing NULL may lead to undefined behavior (e.g., segfault) depending on libc.
Caller owns the returned string and must free it with icalmemory_free_buffer().

functions.name: icalparameter_new
functions.description: Create a new icalparameter of the specified kind. Returns a newly allocated parameter object that the caller must later free. Intended for constructing parameters programmatically.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL on allocation failure (icalerrno set to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR).
The returned object is owned by the caller and must be released with icalparameter_free().
The kind should be a valid icalparameter_kind (recommended to verify with icalparameter_kind_is_valid), though behavior for invalid kinds is not explicitly documented.

functions.name: icalparameter_clone
functions.description: Create a deep copy of an existing icalparameter. Useful when duplicating parameter objects.
requirements: old must be non-NULL; otherwise returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
Caller must check for NULL on allocation/clone failure (may return NULL without setting icalerrno in case of internal clone error).
The returned clone is owned by the caller and must be released with icalparameter_free().

functions.name: icalparameter_new_from_string
functions.description: Parse a string of the form "PARAMNAME=VALUE" to create an icalparameter. Useful for parsing textual iCalendar data into parameter objects.
requirements: str must be non-NULL; otherwise returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
str must be well-formed ("PARAMNAME=VALUE"); malformed input yields NULL with icalerrno set to ICAL_MALFORMEDDATA_ERROR.
On internal allocation/copy failure, returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR.
The returned object is owned by the caller and must be released with icalparameter_free().

functions.name: icalparameter_new_from_value_string
functions.description: Create a new icalparameter of the given kind and set its value from the provided string.
requirements: value must be non-NULL; otherwise returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
The returned object is owned by the caller and must be released with icalparameter_free().
The kind should be an appropriate/valid icalparameter_kind for the value; specifics are not documented.

functions.name: icalparameter_free
functions.description: Free an icalparameter previously created with any icalparameter_new* function or icalparameter_clone. Releases all associated resources.
requirements: parameter must be a parameter object obtained from libical creation/clone APIs.
After calling, the pointer must not be used again.
Behavior on passing NULL is not documented; callers should avoid passing NULL unless known to be accepted by the implementation.

functions.name: icalparameter_as_ical_string
functions.description: Serialize an icalparameter to its RFC 5545/RFC 6868-compliant string form. Returns a pointer to a libical-owned buffer that may be invalidated by the next call into libical.
requirements: parameter must be non-NULL; otherwise returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
The parameter must be recognized and well-formed; otherwise sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR (unrecognized kind) or ICAL_MALFORMEDDATA_ERROR (malformed) and returns NULL.
Do not free the returned string; it is owned by libical and may be reclaimed on the next library call.

functions.name: icalparameter_as_ical_string_r
functions.description: Serialize an icalparameter to its RFC 5545/RFC 6868-compliant string form. Returns a newly allocated buffer owned by the caller.
requirements: parameter must be non-NULL; otherwise returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
The parameter must be recognized and well-formed; otherwise sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR (unrecognized kind) or ICAL_MALFORMEDDATA_ERROR (malformed) and returns NULL.
Caller must free the returned string with icalmemory_free_buffer() when done (do not use free()).

functions.name: icalparameter_isa
functions.description: Return the icalparameter_kind of the given parameter. Utility for introspection and validation of parameter types.
requirements: parameter may be NULL; when NULL, the function returns ICAL_NO_PARAMETER.
The input must be a valid icalparameter object when non-NULL.

functions.name: icalparameter_isa_parameter
functions.description: Determine whether the given libical-origin object is an icalparameter.
requirements: param must originate from libical; passing objects not from libical has undefined behavior.
param may be NULL; when NULL, the function returns 0 (false).

functions.name: icalparameter_set_xname
functions.description: Set the X-name (custom parameter name beginning with "X-") of a parameter. The string is copied by libical.
requirements: param must be non-NULL; if NULL, icalerrno is set to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR (noted as ICAL_BARARG_ERROR in comments).
v must be non-NULL; if NULL, icalerrno is set to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR (noted as ICAL_BARARG_ERROR in comments).
On memory allocation failure, errno is set to ENOMEM.
Caller retains ownership of v; it must remain valid until the function returns.

functions.name: icalparameter_get_xname
functions.description: Get the X-name (custom parameter name) of a parameter. Returns a libical-owned string.
requirements: param must be non-NULL; otherwise returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
Do not free or modify the returned string; it is owned by libical.

functions.name: icalparameter_set_xvalue
functions.description: Set the X-value of a parameter. The string is copied by libical.
requirements: param must be non-NULL; if NULL, icalerrno is set to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR (noted as ICAL_BARARG_ERROR in comments).
v must be non-NULL; if NULL, icalerrno is set to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR (noted as ICAL_BARARG_ERROR in comments).
On memory allocation failure, errno is set to ENOMEM.
Caller retains ownership of v; it must remain valid until the function returns.

functions.name: icalparameter_get_xvalue
functions.description: Get the X-value of a parameter. Returns a libical-owned string.
requirements: param must be non-NULL; otherwise returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
Do not free or modify the returned string; it is owned by libical.

functions.name: icalparameter_set_iana_name
functions.description: Set the IANA-registered name of a parameter. The string is copied by libical.
requirements: param must be non-NULL; if NULL, icalerrno is set to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR (comment references ICAL_BARARG_ERROR).
v must be non-NULL; if NULL, icalerrno is set to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR (comment references ICAL_BARARG_ERROR).
On memory allocation failure, errno is set to ENOMEM.
Caller retains ownership of v; it must remain valid until the function returns.

functions.name: icalparameter_get_iana_name
functions.description: Get the IANA-registered name of a parameter. Returns a libical-owned string.
requirements: param must be non-NULL; otherwise returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
Do not free or modify the returned string; it is owned by libical.

functions.name: icalparameter_set_iana_value
functions.description: Set the IANA value of a parameter. The string is copied by libical.
requirements: param must be non-NULL; if NULL, icalerrno is set to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR (comment references ICAL_BARARG_ERROR).
v must be non-NULL; if NULL, icalerrno is set to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR (comment references ICAL_BARARG_ERROR).
On memory allocation failure, errno is set to ENOMEM.
Caller retains ownership of v; it must remain valid until the function returns.

functions.name: icalparameter_get_iana_value
functions.description: Get the IANA value of a parameter. Returns a libical-owned string.
requirements: param must be non-NULL; otherwise returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
Do not free or modify the returned string; it is owned by libical.

functions.name: icalparameter_has_same_name
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT bool icalparameter_has_same_name(const icalparameter *param1, const icalparameter *param2);
functions.description: Compare two parameters and report whether their names are identical.
requirements: param1 must be non-NULL; if NULL, returns false and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
param2 must be non-NULL; if NULL, returns false and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
No ownership is taken of either parameter.

functions.name: icalparameter_kind_to_string
functions.description: Convert an icalparameter_kind to its string name. Returns a libical-owned string.
requirements: Passing a non-existing/invalid kind results in a NULL return.
Do not free or modify the returned string; it is owned by libical.

functions.name: icalparameter_string_to_kind
functions.description: Parse a string name and return the corresponding icalparameter_kind.
requirements: string may be NULL; when NULL, returns ICAL_NO_PARAMETER.
Depending on ical_get_unknown_token_handling_setting(), unknown strings result in ICAL_NO_PARAMETER or ICAL_IANA_PARAMETER.
Caller retains ownership of the input string.

functions.name: icalparameter_kind_is_valid
functions.description: Check whether the provided icalparameter_kind is valid.
requirements: No special requirements beyond providing a value of type icalparameter_kind.

functions.name: icalparameter_kind_value_kind
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT icalvalue_kind icalparameter_kind_value_kind(const icalparameter_kind kind, int *is_multivalued);
functions.description: Return the icalvalue_kind associated with the given parameter kind and indicate whether the parameter is multivalued via is_multivalued.
requirements: kind must be an icalparameter_kind value; validity expectations are not documented.
is_multivalued is expected to be a writable pointer to int when non-NULL; exact requirements (e.g., whether NULL is allowed) are not documented and thus unknown.

functions.name: icalparameter_is_multivalued
functions.description: Return true if the specified parameter is multivalued.
requirements: param should be a valid icalparameter; behavior and error handling for NULL are not documented and thus unknown.

functions.name: icalparameter_decode_value
functions.description: In-place decode of a parameter value according to RFC 6868 (caret encoding). Intended to convert encoded parameter values to their literal form.
requirements: value should be a non-NULL, writable, NUL-terminated string buffer; function modifies the buffer in place (inferred from purpose and signature).
Exact error handling for NULL or invalid encoding is not documented and thus unknown.

functions.name: icalparser_new
functions.description: Creates a new iCalendar line-oriented parser instance. Use to incrementally parse RFC5545 content lines into icalcomponent objects. Returns NULL on allocation failure (icalerrno set to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR). Free the parser with icalparser_free() when done.
requirements: Caller does not pass any arguments.
On success, the returned icalparser must later be freed with icalparser_free().
On error, the function returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR.

functions.name: icalparser_add_line
functions.description: Adds a single RFC5545 content line to the parser. When the line completes a component, returns that icalcomponent; otherwise returns NULL. On certain errors, sets the parser state to ICALPARSER_ERROR and may return invalid components (e.g., ICAL_XLICINVALID_COMPONENT or components containing ICAL_XLICERROR_PROPERTY). Ownership of the input line transfers to libical.
requirements: parser must be a valid, non-NULL icalparser instance; if NULL, returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
line must be non-NULL; if NULL, returns NULL and sets the parser state to ICALPARSER_ERROR.
line must not be an empty string; if empty, returns NULL.
Ownership of line transfers to libical upon call; the caller must not free or reuse it after passing to this function.
If a non-NULL icalcomponent is returned, the caller owns it and must free it with the appropriate icalcomponent_free() after use.
Caller should check parser state via icalparser_get_state() to detect ICALPARSER_ERROR and/or inspect returned components for error indicator types.

functions.name: icalparser_clean
functions.description: Flushes the parser, clearing internal state and returning any component(s) parsed so far, even if an END tag has not been seen. Inserts X-LIC-ERROR properties on parsing errors. Use to finalize and reset a parser mid-stream.
requirements: parser must be a valid, non-NULL icalparser; if NULL, returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
Returned icalcomponent (if any) is owned by the caller and must be freed with icalcomponent_free() after use.

functions.name: icalparser_get_state
functions.description: Returns the parser’s current state (e.g., ICALPARSER_IN_PROGRESS, ICALPARSER_SUCCESS, ICALPARSER_ERROR, etc.). Use to check parsing status after operations like icalparser_add_line() or icalparser_parse().
requirements: parser must be a valid, non-NULL icalparser pointer.

functions.name: icalparser_free
functions.description: Releases an icalparser object created by icalparser_new(). After this call, the parser must not be used.
requirements: parser must be a valid icalparser previously created by icalparser_new() and not already freed.
After freeing, the parser pointer must not be used.

functions.name: icalparser_parse
functions.description: Message-oriented parsing: reads content lines from the supplied generator function and parses a single icalcomponent. Returns the parsed component, or NULL on error. May set the parser state to ICALPARSER_ERROR and/or produce components that indicate errors via ICAL_XLICINVALID_COMPONENT or ICAL_XLICERROR_PROPERTY. The generator’s third argument ‘d’ is supplied via icalparser_set_gen_data().
requirements: parser must be a valid, non-NULL icalparser; if NULL, returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_BADARG_ERROR.
line_gen_func must be a valid function of type icalparser_line_gen_func that returns one content line per call, NULL on EOF or error.
If the data read by line_gen_func is empty, the function returns NULL.
If line_gen_func returns NULL for a line, the function returns NULL and sets the parser state to ICALPARSER_ERROR.
The caller may optionally set per-call user data via icalparser_set_gen_data(parser, d) prior to calling this function; the generator will receive that pointer as its third parameter.
On success, the returned icalcomponent is owned by the caller and must be freed with the appropriate icalcomponent_free() after use.

functions.name: icalparser_set_gen_data
functions.description: Associates an opaque pointer with the parser that will be provided as the ‘d’ argument to line generator functions used by icalparser_parse() and icalparser_get_line().
requirements: parser should be a valid icalparser (initialized via icalparser_new()).
Caller is responsible for ensuring the lifetime of the data pointer remains valid for the duration of parsing operations that use it.

functions.name: icalparser_parse_string
functions.description: Parses a NUL-terminated string containing iCalendar-formatted data into an icalcomponent. Returns NULL on error and sets icalerrno.
requirements: str should be a valid pointer to iCal formatted data; on error the function returns NULL and sets icalerrno.
On success, the returned icalcomponent is owned by the caller and must be freed with icalcomponent_free() after use.

functions.name: icalparser_get_ctrl
functions.description: Gets the current library-wide setting for how the parser handles CONTROL characters in content lines (KEEP, OMIT, or ERROR).

functions.name: icalparser_set_ctrl
functions.description: Sets the library-wide behavior for handling CONTROL characters in content lines: keep them, omit them, or insert an X-LIC-ERROR line.
requirements: ctrl must be one of the defined icalparser_ctrl values: ICALPARSER_CTRL_KEEP, ICALPARSER_CTRL_OMIT, or ICALPARSER_CTRL_ERROR.

functions.name: icalparser_get_line
functions.description: Reads from the supplied generator until a full content line (including folded continuations) is assembled, then returns that single iCal content line. Returns NULL at end of input. The returned pointer is owned by libical and must not be freed by the caller. The generator’s ‘d’ parameter can be set via icalparser_set_gen_data().
requirements: parser should be a valid icalparser (initialized via icalparser_new()).
line_gen_func must match icalparser_line_gen_func and supply data, returning NULL at EOF.
Caller must not free or modify the returned pointer (it is owned by libical).

functions.name: icalparser_string_line_generator
functions.description: A line generator compatible with icalparser_line_gen_func. Typically used to generate content lines into the provided buffer from a string-like data source referenced by d. Returns a pointer to a single line or NULL at end of data. Specific source semantics are not documented here.
requirements: out should point to a writable buffer of size buf_size bytes (details not explicitly documented).
d is an opaque data pointer whose interpretation depends on this generator’s implementation (details not documented).
Behavioral details (expected encoding, newline handling, and lifetime) are unknown from this header and should be verified against implementation or higher-level docs.

functions.name: icalperiodtype_from_string
functions.description: Parses an iCal-formatted period string into an icalperiodtype. The string may specify either a start and end time or a start time and a duration (e.g., "<STARTTIME>/<ENDTIME>" or "<STARTTIME>/<DURATION>"). On malformed input it signals an error via icalerrno and returns a null period. Use when converting text representations (e.g., from .ics) into a structured period.
requirements: str must contain a properly formatted iCal period: "<STARTTIME>/<ENDTIME>" or "<STARTTIME>/<DURATION>".
Times must use the same format accepted by icaltime_from_string(); durations must use the format accepted by icaldurationtype_from_string().
On malformed input, the function sets icalerrno to ICAL_MALFORMEDDATA_ERROR and returns icalperiodtype_null_period(); callers should check for a null period and/or icalerrno.
Behavior for str == NULL is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: icalperiodtype_as_ical_string
functions.description: Converts an icalperiodtype into an iCal-formatted string. Useful for serializing a period for output (e.g., writing to an .ics file or logging). The returned string is owned by libical and must not be freed by the caller. Allocation failures are reported via icalerrno.
requirements: Input p should represent a valid period (inferred from purpose).
On internal allocation error, the function sets icalerrno to ICAL_ALLOCATION_ERROR; callers should handle this condition.
The returned pointer is owned by libical; the caller must not free() it or otherwise release it.

functions.name: icalperiodtype_as_ical_string_r
functions.description: Converts an icalperiodtype into an iCal-formatted string and returns a caller-owned buffer. Use when you need an independent string that you can manage. Allocation failures are reported via icalerrno. The returned buffer must be released by the caller with the appropriate function (e.g., icalmemory_free_buffer).
requirements: Input p should represent a valid period (inferred from purpose).
On internal allocation error, the function sets icalerrno to ICAL_ALLOCATION_ERROR; callers should handle this condition.
The returned string is owned by the caller and must be released after use with the appropriate function (e.g., icalmemory_free_buffer).

functions.name: icalperiodtype_null_period
functions.description: Creates and returns a null icalperiodtype (start and end times are null; duration is a null duration). Useful as a sentinel value or for initialization.

functions.name: icalperiodtype_is_null_period
functions.description: Returns true if the supplied period is a null period, false otherwise. Use to test whether an icalperiodtype is the sentinel produced by icalperiodtype_null_period().
requirements: p should be an initialized struct icalperiodtype (inferred).

functions.name: icalperiodtype_is_valid_period
functions.description: Returns true if the supplied period is considered a valid period, false otherwise. Use to validate a period before serialization or further processing. Specific validity rules are not documented here.
requirements: Validity criteria are not documented in this header (unknown).
p should be an initialized struct icalperiodtype (inferred).

functions.name: icalproperty_new
functions.description: Creates a new icalproperty of the specified kind. Use when constructing iCalendar properties programmatically.
requirements: kind must be a valid icalproperty_kind (use icalproperty_kind_is_valid to check if needed).
Returned pointer must be freed with icalproperty_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: icalproperty_new_impl
functions.description: Internal/new-implementation variant to create a new icalproperty of the specified kind. Usage is the same as icalproperty_new.
requirements: kind must be a valid icalproperty_kind.
Returned pointer must be freed with icalproperty_free.

functions.name: icalproperty_clone
functions.description: Deeply clones an existing icalproperty and returns a new property. Useful for duplicating properties. Since 4.0.
requirements: old must be a valid, initialized icalproperty pointer.
Returned clone must be freed with icalproperty_free.

functions.name: icalproperty_new_from_string
functions.description: Parses an iCalendar property from its string representation and constructs a new icalproperty.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a valid iCalendar property line.
Returned pointer must be freed with icalproperty_free.
Parsing errors may occur if the string is not a valid property; error handling behavior is not specified here.

functions.name: icalproperty_as_ical_string
functions.description: Serializes the property to its iCalendar text form and returns it as a string.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
Returned pointer is const; caller must not modify or free it. Lifetime/ownership are not specified here and may be internal to the library.

functions.name: icalproperty_as_ical_string_r
functions.description: Re-entrant/alternative serializer that returns the iCalendar text form of the property. Unlike typical “_r” conventions, this returns const char* per the header.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
Returned pointer is const; caller must not modify or free it. Allocation/ownership are not specified in this header.

functions.name: icalproperty_free
functions.description: Frees an icalproperty and any resources owned by it.
requirements: prop must be either NULL or a pointer returned by libical property creation/cloning functions.
Do not use prop after calling this function (dangling pointer).
If prop is NULL, behavior is typically a no-op (not explicitly stated).

functions.name: icalproperty_isa
functions.description: Returns the icalproperty_kind of the given property.
requirements: property must be a valid icalproperty pointer.

functions.name: icalproperty_isa_property
functions.description: Runtime type check: returns true if the given pointer refers to an icalproperty.
requirements: property may be NULL or any pointer; function indicates whether it is an icalproperty.
No ownership is transferred.

functions.name: icalproperty_add_parameters
functions.description: Adds multiple parameters to a property from a va_list. Used for varargs-based parameter addition.
requirements: prop must be a valid pointer to an internal icalproperty_impl (intended for internal/advanced usage).
args must be a valid, initialized va_list containing parameters in the format expected by libical (exact format is not specified here).
Caller is responsible for correctly initializing and ending the va_list in the calling context.

functions.name: icalproperty_add_parameter
functions.description: Adds a parameter to the property (e.g., TZID).
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
parameter must be a valid icalparameter pointer.
Ownership/duplication semantics of parameter are not specified here; do not free parameter unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: icalproperty_set_parameter
functions.description: Sets/replaces a parameter on the property.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
parameter must be a valid icalparameter pointer.
Exact replacement policy and ownership transfer are not specified in this header.

functions.name: icalproperty_set_parameter_from_string
functions.description: Creates/sets a parameter on the property by name and value strings.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a parameter (e.g., "TZID" or an X- param).
value must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string with the parameter value.

functions.name: icalproperty_get_parameter_as_string
functions.description: Gets the value of the named parameter as a string.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated parameter name.
Returned string is const; do not modify or free. Behavior when parameter is not present is not specified here (may return NULL).

functions.name: icalproperty_get_parameter_as_string_r
functions.description: Re-entrant/alternative getter for the named parameter value as a string. Returns const char* per header.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated parameter name.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free. Behavior when missing is not specified.

functions.name: icalproperty_remove_parameter_by_kind
functions.description: Removes all parameters of the specified kind from the property.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
kind must be a valid icalparameter_kind.

functions.name: icalproperty_remove_parameter_by_name
functions.description: Removes all parameters matching the specified name (built-in like TZID or custom X- parameters).
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated parameter name.

functions.name: icalproperty_remove_parameter_by_ref
functions.description: Removes the specific parameter instance (by reference) from the property.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
param must be a valid icalparameter pointer that is currently attached to prop.

functions.name: icalproperty_count_parameters
functions.description: Returns the number of parameters attached to the property.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.

functions.name: icalproperty_get_first_parameter
functions.description: Begins iteration: returns the first parameter of the specified kind for the property.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
kind must be a valid icalparameter_kind.
Do not modify the property's parameter list while iterating.

functions.name: icalproperty_get_next_parameter
functions.description: Continues iteration: returns the next parameter of the specified kind for the property.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
kind must be the same icalparameter_kind used with icalproperty_get_first_parameter for this iteration.
Do not modify the property's parameter list while iterating.

functions.name: icalproperty_set_value
functions.description: Sets the value object for the property.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
value must be a valid icalvalue pointer with a type compatible with the property's kind.
Ownership/duplication behavior of value is not specified in this header.

functions.name: icalproperty_set_value_from_string
functions.description: Parses and sets the property's value from a string, optionally using a given value type.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing the value representation.
type, if not NULL, should be a NUL-terminated string naming the value type (exact accepted names not specified here).
Value must be compatible with the property's kind; parsing errors are possible if not.

functions.name: icalproperty_get_value
functions.description: Returns the icalvalue associated with the property.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
Returned pointer is owned by the property; do not free or modify unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: icalproperty_get_value_as_string
functions.description: Returns the property's value serialized as a string.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
Returned string is const; do not modify or free. May return NULL if no value (not specified).

functions.name: icalproperty_get_value_as_string_r
functions.description: Re-entrant serializer for the property's value; returns a newly allocated string representation.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
Returned char* is caller-owned; free it when no longer needed.

functions.name: icalvalue_set_parent
functions.description: Sets the parent icalproperty for the given icalvalue.
requirements: value must be a valid icalvalue pointer.
property must be a valid icalproperty pointer.

functions.name: icalvalue_get_parent
functions.description: Returns the parent icalproperty for the specified icalvalue. Since 3.0.
requirements: value must be a valid icalvalue pointer.

functions.name: icalproperty_set_x_name
functions.description: Sets the X- property name for this property (used when the kind is an X- property).
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string (e.g., "X-FOO").

functions.name: icalproperty_get_x_name
functions.description: Gets the X- property name for this property.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: icalproperty_get_property_name
functions.description: Returns the property name: the type name as a string, or the X-name for X-properties.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: icalproperty_get_property_name_r
functions.description: Returns the property name as a newly allocated string (re-entrant form).
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
Returned char* is caller-owned; free it when no longer needed.

functions.name: icalparameter_value_to_value_kind
functions.description: Converts an icalparameter_value enumeration to the corresponding icalvalue_kind.
requirements: value must be a valid icalparameter_value.

functions.name: icalparameter_set_parent
functions.description: Sets the parent icalproperty for the specified icalparameter. Since 3.0.
requirements: param must be a valid icalparameter pointer.
property must be a valid icalproperty pointer.

functions.name: icalparameter_get_parent
functions.description: Returns the parent icalproperty for the specified icalparameter. Since 3.0.
requirements: param must be a valid icalparameter pointer.

functions.name: icalproperty_kind_to_value_kind
functions.description: Maps an icalproperty_kind to its default icalvalue_kind.
requirements: kind must be a valid icalproperty_kind.

functions.name: icalproperty_value_kind_to_kind
functions.description: Maps an icalvalue_kind to a corresponding icalproperty_kind.
requirements: kind must be a valid icalvalue_kind.

functions.name: icalproperty_kind_to_string
functions.description: Returns the string name of an icalproperty_kind.
requirements: kind must be a valid icalproperty_kind.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: icalproperty_string_to_kind
functions.description: Parses a property kind name string into an icalproperty_kind.
requirements: string must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated property kind name.

functions.name: icalproperty_kind_is_valid
functions.description: Checks whether a specific icalproperty_kind value is valid.
requirements: kind may be any icalproperty_kind value; returns whether it is valid.

functions.name: icalproperty_string_to_method
functions.description: Parses a METHOD string into an icalproperty_method enum.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated METHOD name string.

functions.name: icalproperty_method_to_string
functions.description: Returns the string name for an icalproperty_method.
requirements: method must be a valid icalproperty_method.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: icalproperty_enum_to_string
functions.description: Returns the string name for a libical enumeration value (context-dependent).
requirements: e must be a valid enumeration value for the relevant context.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: icalproperty_enum_to_string_r
functions.description: Re-entrant form returning a newly allocated string for an enum value.
requirements: e must be a valid enumeration value for the relevant context.
Returned char* is caller-owned; free it when no longer needed.

functions.name: icalproperty_kind_and_string_to_enum
functions.description: Maps a property kind and string to a specific enumeration integer for that kind.
requirements: kind must be a valid icalproperty_kind encoded as int.
str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming an enum value for the given kind.

functions.name: icalproperty_status_to_string
functions.description: Returns the string name for an icalproperty_status.
requirements: Argument must be a valid icalproperty_status value.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: icalproperty_string_to_status
functions.description: Parses a string into an icalproperty_status value.
requirements: string must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated status name.

functions.name: icalproperty_action_to_string
functions.description: Returns the string name for an icalproperty_action.
requirements: Argument must be a valid icalproperty_action value.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: icalproperty_string_to_action
functions.description: Parses a string into an icalproperty_action value.
requirements: string must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated action name.

functions.name: icalproperty_transp_to_string
functions.description: Returns the string name for an icalproperty_transp (transparency).
requirements: Argument must be a valid icalproperty_transp value.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: icalproperty_string_to_transp
functions.description: Parses a string into an icalproperty_transp value.
requirements: string must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated transparency name.

functions.name: icalproperty_class_to_string
functions.description: Returns the string name for an icalproperty_class.
requirements: Argument must be a valid icalproperty_class value.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: icalproperty_string_to_class
functions.description: Parses a string into an icalproperty_class value.
requirements: string must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated class name.

functions.name: icalproperty_participanttype_to_string
functions.description: Returns the string name for an icalproperty_participanttype.
requirements: Argument must be a valid icalproperty_participanttype value.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: icalproperty_string_to_participanttype
functions.description: Parses a string into an icalproperty_participanttype value.
requirements: string must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated participant type name.

functions.name: icalproperty_resourcetype_to_string
functions.description: Returns the string name for an icalproperty_resourcetype.
requirements: Argument must be a valid icalproperty_resourcetype value.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free.

functions.name: icalproperty_string_to_resourcetype
functions.description: Parses a string into an icalproperty_resourcetype value.
requirements: string must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated resource type name.

functions.name: icalproperty_enum_belongs_to_property
functions.description: Checks whether the given enumeration value e belongs to (is valid for) the specified property kind.
requirements: kind must be a valid icalproperty_kind.
e should be an integer value from the appropriate enumeration for the given kind.

functions.name: icalproperty_normalize
functions.description: Normalizes the property by reordering/sorting its parameters. Since 3.0.
requirements: prop must be a valid icalproperty pointer.

functions.name: icalproperty_set_allow_empty_properties
functions.description: Sets global behavior for handling empty properties. If false (default), empty properties are replaced with X-LIC-ERROR. If true, empty properties are allowed. Since 4.0.
requirements: No specific requirements; affects library-wide behavior.
Note: If icalerror_get_errors_are_fatal is true, a SIGABRT will be raised whenever an empty property is encountered (per header note).

functions.name: icalproperty_get_allow_empty_properties
functions.description: Returns whether empty properties are currently allowed (true) or replaced with X-LIC-ERROR (false). Since 4.0.

functions.name: icalproperty_begin_parameter
functions.description: Initializes and returns an iterator (icalparamiter) over parameters of the specified kind for the property.
requirements: property must be a valid icalproperty pointer.
kind must be a valid icalparameter_kind.
Do not modify the property's parameter list during iteration.

functions.name: icalparamiter_next
functions.description: Advances the iterator and returns the next parameter, or NULL when done.
requirements: i must be a valid iterator previously obtained via icalproperty_begin_parameter.
Do not modify the property's parameters during iteration.

functions.name: icalparamiter_deref
functions.description: Returns the current parameter referenced by the iterator (without advancing).
requirements: i must be a valid iterator previously obtained via icalproperty_begin_parameter.

functions.name: icalrecur_string_to_freq
functions.description: Parses a frequency token (e.g., "DAILY", "WEEKLY") into an icalrecurrencetype_frequency enum value.
requirements: str may be NULL only if the implementation tolerates it; otherwise must point to a NUL-terminated C string.
Input should be a valid RFC 5545 FREQ value; otherwise conversion result is implementation-defined (unknown).

functions.name: icalrecur_freq_to_string
functions.description: Converts an icalrecurrencetype_frequency enum value to its canonical string name (e.g., ICAL_DAILY_RECURRENCE -> "DAILY").
requirements: kind must be a valid icalrecurrencetype_frequency enumerator.

functions.name: icalrecur_string_to_skip
functions.description: Parses a skip policy token for RSCALE (e.g., "BACKWARD", "FORWARD", "OMIT") into an icalrecurrencetype_skip enum value.
requirements: str should be a valid skip keyword as per RFC 7529; otherwise result is implementation-defined (unknown).
str must point to a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: icalrecur_skip_to_string
functions.description: Converts an icalrecurrencetype_skip enum value to its canonical string name.
requirements: kind must be a valid icalrecurrencetype_skip enumerator.

functions.name: icalrecur_weekday_to_string
functions.description: Converts an icalrecurrencetype_weekday enum value to its string abbreviation (e.g., ICAL_MONDAY_WEEKDAY -> "MO").
requirements: kind must be a valid icalrecurrencetype_weekday enumerator.

functions.name: icalrecur_string_to_weekday
functions.description: Parses a weekday abbreviation (e.g., "MO", "TU") into an icalrecurrencetype_weekday enum value.
requirements: str must point to a NUL-terminated C string.
str should be a valid weekday token; otherwise conversion result is implementation-defined (unknown).

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_new
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new icalrecurrencetype instance with refcount set to 1.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL (allocation failure).
Returned object must be released with icalrecurrencetype_unref when no longer needed.

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of the given icalrecurrencetype.
requirements: recur must be a valid pointer to an initialized icalrecurrencetype.
Reference increments must be balanced with corresponding icalrecurrencetype_unref calls.

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_unref
functions.description: Decrements the reference count; when it reaches zero, frees the instance and its owned memory (rscale and BY* arrays).
requirements: recur must be a valid pointer to a previously initialized icalrecurrencetype.
Do not use recur after a call that reduces its refcount to zero.
Each successful icalrecurrencetype_ref must be matched by a corresponding icalrecurrencetype_unref.

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_rscale_supported_calendars
functions.description: Returns an array of RSCALE-supported calendar identifiers. Specific contents and element types are not described in this header (unknown).
requirements: Caller must treat the returned icalarray according to libical ownership rules (unknown from this header).
Do not assume mutability or lifetime; consult implementation or library docs (unknown).

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_clone
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of the given recurrence rule. The clone has refcount 1.
requirements: r must be a valid pointer to an initialized icalrecurrencetype.
Caller must check for NULL return (allocation failure).
The returned clone must be released with icalrecurrencetype_unref when no longer needed.

functions.name: icalrecur_resize_by
functions.description: Resizes the buffer backing an icalrecurrence_by_data entry (BY* arrays). If size is 0, frees the buffer.
requirements: by must point to a valid icalrecurrence_by_data structure.
size must be >= 0.
Caller must check the boolean return for success before using the resized storage.

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_day_day_of_week
functions.description: Decodes an encoded BYDAY value to its weekday (1=Monday,...,7=Sunday). Position 0 denotes 'any/every'.
requirements: day must be an encoded value as stored in by[ICAL_BY_DAY]; otherwise result is unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_day_position
functions.description: Decodes an encoded BYDAY value to its ordinal position within the period (e.g., 1=first, -1=last, 0=any/every).
requirements: day must be an encoded value as stored in by[ICAL_BY_DAY]; otherwise result is unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_encode_day
functions.signature: short icalrecurrencetype_encode_day(enum icalrecurrencetype_weekday weekday, int position);
functions.description: Encodes a weekday and ordinal position into a value suitable for storage in by[ICAL_BY_DAY].
requirements: weekday should be a valid icalrecurrencetype_weekday (MO..SU); ICAL_NO_WEEKDAY is likely not meaningful for encoding (unknown).
position 0 denotes 'any/every'; positive for Nth, negative for Nth-from-end. Range limits are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_month_is_leap
functions.description: Checks whether an encoded BYMONTH value has the RSCALE 'L' (leap) suffix set.
requirements: month must be an encoded BYMONTH value as stored in by[ICAL_BY_MONTH].

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_month_month
functions.description: Extracts the numeric month from an encoded BYMONTH value (the 'L' bit, if any, is ignored).
requirements: month must be an encoded BYMONTH value as stored in by[ICAL_BY_MONTH].

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_encode_month
functions.description: Encodes a numeric month and leap-suffix flag into a value suitable for storage in by[ICAL_BY_MONTH].
requirements: month should be a valid month number for the target calendar; valid range is not specified here (unknown).
is_leap indicates the RFC 7529 'L' suffix.

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_new_from_string
functions.description: Parses an RRULE string (RFC 5545/7529) into a newly allocated icalrecurrencetype with refcount 1.
requirements: str must be a NUL-terminated C string containing a valid RRULE; invalid input handling may depend on ical_get_invalid_rrule_handling_setting().
Caller must check for NULL return (parse/allocation failure).
Returned object must be released with icalrecurrencetype_unref when no longer needed.

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_as_string
functions.description: Serializes a recurrence rule to an RRULE string. Memory ownership details are not specified here (unknown).
requirements: recur must be a valid pointer to an initialized icalrecurrencetype.
Caller should check for NULL return (allocation failure).
Ownership/lifetime of returned string is not specified in this header; consult libical docs (unknown).

functions.name: icalrecurrencetype_as_string_r
functions.description: Reentrant form of serialization to an RRULE string. Memory ownership details are not specified here (unknown).
requirements: recur must be a valid pointer to an initialized icalrecurrencetype.
Caller should check for NULL return (allocation failure).
Ownership/lifetime of returned string is not specified in this header; consult libical docs (unknown).

functions.name: icalrecur_iterator_new
functions.description: Creates a new iterator over occurrences defined by rule, starting at DTSTART. The iterator may keep a reference to rule; the rule must not be modified while the iterator is in use.
requirements: rule must point to a valid icalrecurrencetype.
dtstart must be a valid icaltimetype (timezone determines iterator output TZ).
Caller must check for NULL return (allocation failure).
Do not modify rule while the iterator exists (explicit).
Iterator must be released with icalrecur_iterator_free.

functions.name: icalrecur_iterator_set_start
functions.description: Sets the iterator start date-time to a value between DTSTART and UNTIL. Cannot be used with COUNT-based RRULEs.
requirements: impl must be a valid iterator created by icalrecur_iterator_new.
The rule must not contain COUNT (explicit).
start must be within [DTSTART, UNTIL] when UNTIL is present (explicit).
Caller must check boolean return for success.

functions.name: icalrecur_iterator_set_end
functions.description: Sets an upper bound; occurrences equal to or after end will not be returned.
requirements: impl must be a valid iterator created by icalrecur_iterator_new.
Caller must check boolean return for success.

functions.name: icalrecur_iterator_set_range
functions.signature: bool icalrecur_iterator_set_range(icalrecur_iterator *impl, struct icaltimetype from, struct icaltimetype to);
functions.description: Sets the iteration range. If to is null time, iteration proceeds forward up to UNTIL (if present) or to the year 2582; if to > from, iterates forward up to and including to; if to < from, configures reverse iteration from from down to and including to. Cannot be used with COUNT-based RRULEs.
requirements: impl must be a valid iterator created by icalrecur_iterator_new.
The rule must not contain COUNT (explicit).
from must be between DTSTART and UNTIL (explicit).
If to is non-null and earlier than from, reverse iteration is used; both bounds inclusive as described (explicit).
Caller must check boolean return for success.

functions.name: icalrecur_iterator_next
functions.description: Advances the iterator and returns the next occurrence. Returns a null time when no further occurrences exist. Returned time is in the same timezone as DTSTART.
requirements: Iterator pointer must be valid.
Caller must check for null time using icaltime_is_null_time to detect exhaustion (as shown in example).

functions.name: icalrecur_iterator_prev
functions.description: Moves the iterator backward and returns the previous occurrence. Returns a null time when no further occurrences exist. Available when reverse iteration is configured.
requirements: Iterator pointer must be valid.
Caller must check for null time using icaltime_is_null_time to detect exhaustion.
Reverse iteration must have been set via icalrecur_iterator_set_range with to < from (explicit).

functions.name: icalrecur_iterator_free
functions.description: Frees a recurrence iterator created by icalrecur_iterator_new.
requirements: Pointer must be a valid iterator or NULL (NULL handling is unknown).
Do not use the iterator after this call.

functions.name: icalrecur_expand_recurrence
functions.signature: bool icalrecur_expand_recurrence(const char *rule, icaltime_t start, int count, icaltime_t *array);
functions.description: Expands an RRULE starting at start into up to count occurrence times in seconds since the POSIX epoch, stored in array. Times are returned in UTC; calculations are done in local time, so convert back to local time if needed.
requirements: rule must be a NUL-terminated RRULE string.
array must point to writable storage for at least count icaltime_t entries.
count must be >= 0.
Caller must check boolean return for success.
Start is an icaltime_t representing DTSTART.

functions.name: ical_get_invalid_rrule_handling_setting
functions.description: Returns the current library setting for handling invalid RRULE BYxxx combinations (treat as error vs ignore).

functions.name: ical_set_invalid_rrule_handling_setting
functions.description: Sets how the library should handle RRULEs with invalid BYxxx combinations.
requirements: newSetting must be a valid ical_invalid_rrule_handling enumerator (ICAL_RRULE_TREAT_AS_ERROR or ICAL_RRULE_IGNORE_INVALID).

functions.name: icalrestriction_compare
functions.description: Evaluate whether a given occurrence count satisfies the specified iCalendar restriction kind. Typical usage: call with the restriction rule you want to enforce (e.g., ICAL_RESTRICTION_ONEPLUS) and the observed count of properties/components; receive true if the count meets the rule, false otherwise. Notes: ICAL_RESTRICTION_NONE always evaluates to false per the documented example; the icalrestriction_kind enum ordering is significant internally but not relevant to callers.
requirements: restr must be a valid value of icalrestriction_kind (explicit).
count represents a quantity; it should be non-negative (inferred: counts cannot be negative).
Caller should not assume side effects; the function is a pure check returning a boolean (inferred from signature and description).
Caller should interpret the boolean return directly; no error code or errno is mentioned for this function (explicit from lack of error handling note).

functions.name: icalrestriction_check
functions.description: Check whether a VCALENDAR component conforms to all restrictions imposed by the iCalendar standard. Pass a pointer to a VCALENDAR icalcomponent; the function returns true if it meets the standard’s restrictions, false otherwise. On invalid input (NULL or non-VCALENDAR), the function returns false and sets icalerrno.
requirements: comp must be non-NULL (explicit: returns false and sets icalerrno if NULL).
comp must be a VCALENDAR component (explicit: returns false and sets icalerrno if not a VCALENDAR).
Caller must check the boolean return value to determine success/failure (explicit).
On failure, caller should examine icalerrno for error details (explicit).
The function does not document modifying comp; callers should not rely on side effects (inferred from purpose and signature).

functions.name: icalstrarray_new
functions.description: Creates a new icalstrarray (array of C strings). This is a macro wrapper around icalarray_new(sizeof(char *), increment_size). Pass 0 to use the library’s default increment size. On allocation failure, returns NULL and sets icalerrno to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR. The caller owns the returned array and must free it with icalstrarray_free().
requirements: increment_size may be 0 to use the library default; otherwise it should be a non-negative size_t value.
On NULL return, the caller must handle the error (icalerrno set to ICAL_NEWFAILED_ERROR).
The returned array must be freed with icalstrarray_free() when no longer needed.
The array pointer must not be used after it has been freed.

functions.name: icalstrarray_element_at
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the string stored at the given position in the array. If array is NULL or the position is not set, returns NULL. The returned string is owned by the array and must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: array must be a valid icalstrarray pointer or NULL.
position must refer to a set slot in the array; otherwise the function returns NULL.
The returned string is owned by the array and must not be freed or modified by the caller.

functions.name: icalstrarray_size
functions.description: Returns the number of strings stored in the array. If array is NULL, returns 0.
requirements: array may be NULL; in that case the function returns 0.

functions.name: icalstrarray_find
functions.description: Finds the first occurrence of needle in array using byte-wise string comparison. Returns the slot index of the first match; if not found or on NULL inputs, returns icalstrarray_size(array).
requirements: array must be a valid icalstrarray pointer or NULL.
needle must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string; if NULL, the function behaves as not found.
Callers should compare the return value against icalstrarray_size(array) to detect a non-match.

functions.name: icalstrarray_append
functions.description: Appends elem to the array without checking for duplicates. If array or elem is NULL, the function does nothing (noop).
requirements: array must be a valid icalstrarray pointer or NULL.
elem must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string; if NULL, the function is a noop.
This function does not prevent duplicates; use icalstrarray_add() to avoid duplicates.

functions.name: icalstrarray_add
functions.description: Appends elem to the array only if no byte-equal string is already present. If array or elem is NULL, the function does nothing (noop).
requirements: array must be a valid icalstrarray pointer or NULL.
elem must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string; if NULL, the function is a noop.

functions.name: icalstrarray_remove_element_at
functions.description: Removes the string at the specified position. If array is NULL or position is greater than or equal to the count, the function does nothing (noop).
requirements: array must be a valid icalstrarray pointer or NULL.
position should be less than icalstrarray_size(array); otherwise the function is a noop.

functions.name: icalstrarray_remove
functions.description: Removes all occurrences of the given string from the array (byte-wise comparison). If array or del is NULL, the function does nothing (noop).
requirements: array must be a valid icalstrarray pointer or NULL.
del must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated C string; if NULL, the function is a noop.

functions.name: icalstrarray_free
functions.description: Frees the array and all its string elements. If array is NULL, this is a noop.
requirements: array must be a pointer returned by icalstrarray_new() or otherwise a valid icalstrarray allocation.
After calling, the array pointer must not be used again.

functions.name: icalstrarray_sort
functions.description: Sorts the array’s strings in ascending order using byte-wise comparison. If array is NULL, this is a noop.
requirements: array must be a valid icalstrarray pointer or NULL.

functions.name: icalstrarray_clone
functions.description: Creates and returns an independent copy of the array and all its strings. If array is NULL, returns NULL. The caller owns the returned clone and must free it with icalstrarray_free().
requirements: array may be NULL; if NULL, the function returns NULL.
On success, the returned array must be freed with icalstrarray_free() when no longer needed.
On NULL return, the caller must handle the error/absence of input appropriately (no specific errno is documented here).

functions.name: icaltime_null_time
functions.description: Constructor returning a null time (no time set). Represents the beginning of the epoch and acts as a sentinel for “unset” time values. Useful to initialize variables before assigning real times.
requirements: No arguments.
Returned struct is a valid icaltimetype representing a null time.

functions.name: icaltime_null_date
functions.description: Constructor returning a null date (no date set). Acts as a sentinel for “unset” date values.
requirements: No arguments.
Returned struct is a valid icaltimetype representing a null date.

functions.name: icaltime_current_time_with_zone
functions.description: Convenience constructor returning the current time in the given timezone as an icaltimetype.
requirements: zone must be a valid timezone pointer; behavior for NULL is not specified.
The returned time is a DATE-TIME (not a DATE).

functions.name: icaltime_today
functions.description: Convenience constructor returning the current day as an icaltimetype with is_date set (DATE). Time fields are date-only.
requirements: No arguments.
Returned object has is_date set (DATE).

functions.name: icaltime_from_timet_with_zone
functions.signature: struct icaltimetype icaltime_from_timet_with_zone(const icaltime_t tm, const bool is_date, const icaltimezone *zone)
functions.description: Constructor building an icaltimetype from seconds since the UNIX epoch, optionally as DATE and with an associated timezone. If zone is NULL the time is floating. If is_date is true the result is a DATE; otherwise DATE-TIME.
requirements: tm is a time value expressed as seconds since UNIX epoch.
If is_date is true, the result is a DATE; callers should not expect time-of-day fields to matter.
If zone is NULL, the time is floating; if non-NULL, it becomes the native timezone of the object.

functions.name: icaltime_from_string
functions.description: Parses an RFC5545/ISO-8601-2004 DATE-TIME string into an icaltimetype. Accepted forms include: "YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS", "YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ", and "TZID=Area/Location:YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS".
requirements: str must point to a valid DATE-TIME per RFC5545 (ISO-8601-2004).
Examples of accepted inputs: DATE with local time, DATE with UTC time (Z), DATE with local time and TZID reference.
Behavior on invalid strings is not documented; callers should validate inputs.

functions.name: icaltime_from_day_of_year
functions.signature: struct icaltimetype icaltime_from_day_of_year(const int doy, const int year)
functions.description: Creates a date (DATE) from a day-of-year and year. Jan 1 is day 1.
requirements: doy is counted from 1 (Jan 1 = 1).
Valid range of doy depends on whether year is a leap year (1..365 or 1..366).
year is a calendar year (e.g., 2001).

functions.name: icaltime_as_timet
functions.description: Returns time as seconds since the UNIX epoch with no timezone conversion. Intended for UTC inputs; otherwise result likely differs from expectation. Prefer icaltime_as_timet_with_zone() when conversion is needed.
requirements: tt should be in UTC if you expect epoch seconds in UTC (no conversion is performed).
Defined return range: if time_t is 64-bit, valid for dates in [1902-01-01, 10000-01-01); if 32-bit, valid up to 2038-01-18 (exclusive).

functions.name: icaltime_as_timet_with_zone
functions.signature: icaltime_t icaltime_as_timet_with_zone(const struct icaltimetype tt, const icaltimezone *zone)
functions.description: Returns time as seconds since UNIX epoch after converting tt to the given timezone. If zone is NULL, no conversion is performed; the value is returned in tt’s native timezone.
requirements: If zone is non-NULL, it must reference a valid timezone; the time is converted to that zone before conversion to epoch seconds.
If zone is NULL, no conversion is performed.

functions.name: icaltime_as_ical_string
functions.description: Formats tt as an RFC5545-compliant string. The created string is owned by libical.
requirements: Caller must not free or modify the returned string (owned by libical).
The pointer may be invalidated by subsequent libical operations that reuse internal buffers (not documented here); copy if persistence is required.

functions.name: icaltime_as_ical_string_r
functions.description: Formats tt as an RFC5545-compliant string. The returned string is owned by the caller.
requirements: Caller owns the returned memory and is responsible for freeing it when no longer needed (exact allocator not specified here).

functions.name: icaltime_get_timezone
functions.description: Returns the timezone associated with t, or NULL if t is floating or a DATE with no timezone.
requirements: t must be an initialized icaltimetype.
Returned pointer may be NULL for floating times.

functions.name: icaltime_get_tzid
functions.description: Returns the tzid string of t’s timezone, or NULL for floating time.
requirements: t must be an initialized icaltimetype.
Returned pointer may be NULL for floating times.

functions.name: icaltime_set_timezone
functions.signature: struct icaltimetype icaltime_set_timezone(struct icaltimetype *t, const icaltimezone *zone)
functions.description: Returns a copy of t that is interpreted relative to zone without applying offset adjustments. For DATE values, timezone is not modified and the result is an exact copy. Use icaltime_convert_to_zone() for true timezone conversion with offsets.
requirements: t must be non-NULL and point to a valid icaltimetype.
zone must be a valid, non-NULL timezone pointer (behavior for NULL not documented).
If t is a DATE, timezone is not changed; the result equals *t.

functions.name: icaltime_day_of_year
functions.description: Returns the day-of-year for t, counting from 1 (Jan 1 = 1).
requirements: t must be an initialized icaltimetype representing a calendar date.

functions.name: icaltime_day_of_week
functions.description: Returns the day of week for t. Sunday is 1, Saturday is 7.
requirements: t must be an initialized icaltimetype representing a calendar date.

functions.name: icaltime_start_doy_week
functions.signature: int icaltime_start_doy_week(const struct icaltimetype t, int fdow)
functions.description: Returns the day-of-year for the first day of the week that contains t. The documentation elsewhere mentions Sunday as the first day, but this function also takes fdow (first day of week). Details of fdow’s accepted range/mapping are not specified here.
requirements: t must be an initialized icaltimetype.
fdow indicates the first day of week; the valid range and mapping (e.g., 1=Sunday) are not documented in this header and are therefore unknown. Callers should consult libical documentation.

functions.name: icaltime_is_null_time
functions.description: Returns true if t is a null time (no time set).
requirements: t must be an icaltimetype; no additional constraints.

functions.name: icaltime_is_valid_time
functions.description: Returns false if t is clearly invalid (but not null), usually from an uncleared or improperly initialized structure or illegal flag values.
requirements: t should be initialized before use; otherwise this may return false.

functions.name: icaltime_is_date
functions.description: Returns true if t represents a DATE (date-only), false if DATE-TIME.
requirements: t must be an initialized icaltimetype.

functions.name: icaltime_is_utc
functions.description: Returns true if t is relative to the UTC timezone. Note: the comment indicates this should only check the zone.
requirements: t must be an initialized icaltimetype.

functions.name: icaltime_compare
functions.signature: int icaltime_compare(const struct icaltimetype a, const struct icaltimetype b)
functions.description: Compares two times after converting both to UTC. Returns -1 if a<b, 0 if equal, 1 if a>b.
requirements: a and b must be valid icaltimetype values with sensible fields.
Timezone conversion to UTC is performed internally.

functions.name: icaltime_compare_date_only
functions.signature: int icaltime_compare_date_only(const struct icaltimetype a, const struct icaltimetype b)
functions.description: Compares only the date components of a and b after converting both to UTC. Returns -1, 0, or 1.
requirements: a and b must be valid icaltimetype values.
Only the date components are considered; times are ignored.

functions.name: icaltime_compare_date_only_tz
functions.signature: int icaltime_compare_date_only_tz(const struct icaltimetype a, const struct icaltimetype b, icaltimezone *tz)
functions.description: Compares only the date components of a and b after converting both to the given timezone. Returns -1, 0, or 1.
requirements: tz must be a valid, non-NULL timezone pointer (no NULL handling documented).
a and b must be valid icaltimetype values.

functions.name: icaltime_adjust
functions.signature: void icaltime_adjust(struct icaltimetype *tt, const int days, const int hours, const int minutes, const int seconds)
functions.description: Adds or subtracts the specified days, hours, minutes, and seconds to/from tt in place. Similar to icaltimezone_adjust_change() but operates on icaltimetype.
requirements: tt must be non-NULL and point to a valid icaltimetype.
days/hours/minutes/seconds may be negative to subtract; no documented bounds.

functions.name: icaltime_normalize
functions.signature: struct icaltimetype icaltime_normalize(const struct icaltimetype tt)
functions.description: Normalizes tt so that all components fall within their normal ranges (e.g., 70 minutes becomes 10 minutes and hour incremented). Useful after arithmetic that causes overflow/underflow.
requirements: tt may contain out-of-range fields; function will normalize them.
Returned value is the normalized time; the input is not modified (passed by value).

functions.name: icaltime_convert_to_zone
functions.signature: struct icaltimetype icaltime_convert_to_zone(const struct icaltimetype tt, icaltimezone *zone)
functions.description: Converts tt from its native timezone to zone and updates the timezone. For DATE values, timezone is not changed and the result equals tt. For floating times, the result represents the same wall time relative to zone.
requirements: zone must be a valid, non-NULL timezone pointer.
If tt is a DATE, no conversion is performed and timezone is not modified.
If tt is floating, the same wall time is returned relative to zone; otherwise, a proper timezone conversion is applied.

functions.name: icaltime_days_in_month
functions.signature: int icaltime_days_in_month(const int month, const int year)
functions.description: Returns the number of days in the specified month of the given year.
requirements: month should be in the range 1..12 (inferred).
year is a calendar year (e.g., 2001).

functions.name: icaltime_is_leap_year
functions.description: Returns true if year is a leap year.
requirements: year is the calendar year (e.g., 2001).

functions.name: icaltime_days_in_year
functions.description: Returns the number of days in year (365 or 366).
requirements: year is the calendar year (e.g., 2001).

functions.name: icaltime_span_new
functions.signature: struct icaltime_span icaltime_span_new(struct icaltimetype dtstart, struct icaltimetype dtend, bool is_busy)
functions.description: Builds an icaltime_span from the given start, end and busy flag. The times in the span are specified in UTC.
requirements: dtstart and dtend should represent UTC instants (per note).
is_busy is a boolean flag (false/true).
Relative ordering of dtstart <= dtend is not documented; callers should ensure consistency.

functions.name: icaltime_span_overlaps
functions.description: Returns true if the two spans overlap or are equal; returns false for adjacent, non-overlapping spans.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be non-NULL pointers to valid spans.
Spans are considered overlapping if s1.start or s1.end lies within s2, or if the spans are equal. Adjacent spans are not overlapping.

functions.name: icaltime_span_contains
functions.description: Returns true if span s lies entirely within container.
requirements: s and container must be non-NULL pointers to valid spans.

functions.name: icaltimezone_new
functions.description: Creates and returns a new icaltimezone object. Use this to allocate a standalone timezone instance managed by the caller.
requirements: Caller must free the object with icaltimezone_free(zone, 1) when no longer needed to avoid memory leaks.
Returned pointer may be NULL only under allocation failure (not documented); callers should handle NULL defensively.

functions.name: icaltimezone_copy
functions.description: Creates a copy of an existing icaltimezone and returns a pointer to the new instance.
requirements: originalzone must be a valid, initialized icaltimezone pointer.
Caller must free the returned copy with icaltimezone_free(copy, 1) when no longer needed.
Returned pointer may be NULL only under allocation failure (not documented); callers should handle NULL defensively.

functions.name: icaltimezone_free
functions.description: Frees memory used by an icaltimezone. If free_struct is non-zero, the icaltimezone struct itself is freed as well.
requirements: zone must be a valid pointer to an icaltimezone previously obtained by icaltimezone_new(), icaltimezone_copy(), or equivalent.
Pass free_struct != 0 only for heap-allocated timezone structs owned by the caller; passing non-zero for built-in or non-owned objects may be invalid (inferred).
Do not use zone after calling this with free_struct != 0.

functions.name: icaltimezone_set_tzid_prefix
functions.description: Sets the prefix used for TZIDs generated from system tzdata. No validation is performed; the caller must ensure correctness. The buffer must remain valid for the lifetime of use.
requirements: new_prefix must begin and end with '/' and be globally unique (e.g., a domain you own).
new_prefix must be less than 256 characters.
Do not change or de-allocate the new_prefix buffer after calling; it must remain valid.
If not set, the library default "/freeassociation.sourceforge.net/" is used.
No error/sanity checking is performed; callers must ensure the provided string is properly formatted.

functions.name: icaltimezone_tzid_prefix
functions.description: Returns the current TZID prefix used for system tzdata-derived TZIDs. The returned pointer is owned by the library.
requirements: Do not free or modify the returned pointer.

functions.name: icaltimezone_free_builtin_timezones
functions.description: Releases memory associated with the library’s built-in timezone data.
requirements: Should only be called when no references to built-in icaltimezone objects are in use (not explicitly documented; standard safety practice).

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_builtin_timezones
functions.description: Returns an icalarray containing one icaltimezone for each built-in timezone. Loads and parses zones.tab to get names and coordinates; does not load VTIMEZONE data.
requirements: Caller must not assume VTIMEZONE components are loaded for returned entries.
Returned icalarray ownership/lifetime is managed by the library (not specified); callers should treat it as read-only unless documentation elsewhere specifies freeing.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_builtin_timezone
functions.description: Returns a single built-in timezone by its Olson location name (e.g., "America/New_York").
requirements: location must be a valid Olson location string. Unknown locations may return NULL (not explicitly stated; inferred).
Returned pointer refers to a built-in timezone; do not free the struct with free_struct != 0.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_builtin_timezone_from_offset
