functions.description: Returns a built-in timezone that matches the given UTC offset (seconds) and optional tzname.
requirements: offset is an offset in seconds from UTC (positive east of UTC, negative west, inferred from standard conventions).
tzname may be used to disambiguate multiple zones with the same offset; may be NULL (not specified; inferred).
Returned pointer refers to a built-in timezone; do not free the struct with free_struct != 0.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_builtin_timezone_from_tzid
functions.description: Returns a built-in timezone that matches the given TZID.
requirements: tzid must be a valid TZID string. Unknown TZIDs may return NULL (not explicitly stated; inferred).
Returned pointer refers to a built-in timezone; do not free the struct with free_struct != 0.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_utc_timezone
functions.description: Returns the UTC timezone object.
requirements: Returned pointer is managed by the library; do not free the struct with free_struct != 0.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_tzid
functions.description: Returns the TZID string for the given timezone.
requirements: zone must be a valid icaltimezone pointer.
Do not free or modify the returned string.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_location
functions.description: Returns the city/location name for the given timezone.
requirements: zone must be a valid icaltimezone pointer.
Do not free or modify the returned string.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_tznames
functions.description: Returns the TZNAMEs used in the latest STANDARD and DAYLIGHT components. If identical, returns a single name (e.g., "LMT"). If different, returns a composite like "EST/EDT". May return NULL.
requirements: zone must be a valid icaltimezone pointer.
Do not free or modify the returned string. It may be NULL; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_latitude
functions.description: Returns the latitude of a built-in timezone in degrees.
requirements: zone must be a valid icaltimezone pointer.
Only meaningful for built-in timezones.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_longitude
functions.description: Returns the longitude of a built-in timezone in degrees.
requirements: zone must be a valid icaltimezone pointer.
Only meaningful for built-in timezones.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_component
functions.description: Returns the VTIMEZONE component associated with the timezone.
requirements: zone must be a valid icaltimezone pointer.
Returned component is owned by the timezone; do not free it directly (usual ownership pattern; not explicitly stated).

functions.name: icaltimezone_set_component
functions.description: Sets the timezone’s VTIMEZONE component and initializes tzid, location, and tzname fields from it. Returns true on success, false if no TZID was found in the component.
requirements: zone must be a valid icaltimezone pointer.
comp must be a VTIMEZONE icalcomponent containing a TZID property.
Caller should check the boolean return value and handle failure if TZID is missing.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_display_name
functions.description: Returns a human-friendly display name for the timezone, preferring the Olson city name, then TZNAME, then TZID. Never returns an empty string. Do not free the returned string.
requirements: zone must be a valid icaltimezone pointer.
Caller must not free or modify the returned string.

functions.name: icaltimezone_convert_time
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT void icaltimezone_convert_time(struct icaltimetype *tt, icaltimezone *from_zone, icaltimezone *to_zone);
functions.description: Converts (rotates) the given time from one timezone to another in-place. If tt only represents a date (no time), no conversion is performed. Any timezone embedded in tt is ignored. If from_zone is NULL, no conversion is performed. If to_zone is NULL, the time is converted to UTC.
requirements: tt must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized struct icaltimetype.
from_zone may be NULL to skip conversion; otherwise must be a valid timezone.
to_zone may be NULL to convert to UTC; otherwise must be a valid timezone.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_utc_offset
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT int icaltimezone_get_utc_offset(icaltimezone *zone, const struct icaltimetype *tt, int *is_daylight);
functions.description: Calculates the UTC offset of a given local time in the specified timezone. Returns the number of seconds to add to UTC to obtain local time. Sets is_daylight to 1 if daylight saving time applies.
requirements: zone must be a valid icaltimezone pointer.
tt must be a valid pointer to an initialized local-time icaltimetype.
If is_daylight is non-NULL, it will be set to 0 or 1 (not explicitly stated; handling NULL is prudent).
Caller must interpret the return value as seconds to add to UTC.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_utc_offset_of_utc_time
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT int icaltimezone_get_utc_offset_of_utc_time(icaltimezone *zone, const struct icaltimetype *tt, int *is_daylight);
functions.description: Calculates the UTC offset for a given UTC time in the specified timezone. Returns seconds to add to UTC to get local time. Sets is_daylight to 1 if daylight saving time applies.
requirements: zone must be a valid icaltimezone pointer.
tt must be a valid pointer to an initialized UTC icaltimetype.
If is_daylight is non-NULL, it will be set to 0 or 1 (not explicitly stated; handling NULL is prudent).
Caller must interpret the return value as seconds to add to UTC.

functions.name: icaltimezone_array_new
functions.description: Creates a new icalarray intended to hold icaltimezone entries (internal-use oriented).
requirements: Caller is responsible for freeing the array with icaltimezone_array_free() when appropriate (not explicitly stated; inferred from presence of free function).

functions.name: icaltimezone_array_append_from_vtimezone
functions.description: Appends timezone entries parsed from the given VTIMEZONE component into the provided icalarray (primarily for internal use).
requirements: timezones must be a valid icalarray created for timezones.
child must be a valid VTIMEZONE icalcomponent.

functions.name: icaltimezone_array_free
functions.description: Frees an icalarray of timezones created by icaltimezone_array_new().
requirements: timezones must be an icalarray previously returned by icaltimezone_array_new().
Do not use timezones after calling this.

functions.name: icaltimezone_expand_vtimezone
functions.description: Expands a VTIMEZONE component into a list of timezone change instances up to the given end_year, storing results in changes.
requirements: comp must be a valid VTIMEZONE icalcomponent.
end_year specifies the inclusive upper bound year for expansion.
changes must be a valid icalarray provided by the caller to receive results.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_location_from_vtimezone
functions.description: Extracts the LOCATION or X-LIC-LOCATION value from a VTIMEZONE component and returns it as a newly allocated string.
requirements: component must be a valid VTIMEZONE icalcomponent.
Caller must free the returned string.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_tznames_from_vtimezone
functions.description: Returns the TZNAMEs used in the last STANDARD and DAYLIGHT components of a VTIMEZONE. If they are the same, returns a single name; otherwise returns a combined string like "EST/EDT". The caller must free the returned string.
requirements: component must be a valid VTIMEZONE icalcomponent.
Caller must free the returned string.

functions.name: icaltimezone_truncate_vtimezone
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT void icaltimezone_truncate_vtimezone(icalcomponent *vtz, icaltimetype start, icaltimetype end, int ms_compatible);
functions.description: Truncates a VTIMEZONE component to the provided start and end times. If either time is null, no truncation occurs at that boundary. If non-null, start and end MUST be specified as UTC. If start is non-null and ms_compatible is 0, RRULE DTSTART values will be adjusted to occur after start. Since 3.0.6.
requirements: vtz must be a valid VTIMEZONE icalcomponent.
If start is provided (non-null), it MUST be UTC.
If end is provided (non-null), it MUST be UTC.
ms_compatible == 0 allows adjustment of RRULE DTSTART after the start time; callers should set accordingly.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_system_zone_directory
functions.description: Returns the full path to the system zoneinfo directory (where zone.tab resides). The returned pointer refers to static memory and must not be freed. If TZDIR is set in the environment, it is searched first; otherwise well-known system paths are checked. Since 4.0.
requirements: Do not free or modify the returned string.
Behavior depends on the environment variable TZDIR and system installation paths.

functions.name: icaltimezone_set_system_zone_directory
functions.description: Sets the full path to the system zoneinfo directory (zone.tab must be present there). Passing NULL or an empty string clears the internal zoneinfo path. Since 4.0.
requirements: zonepath should be a valid absolute path to a zoneinfo directory containing zone.tab.
Passing NULL or empty string clears the internal path.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_zone_directory
functions.description: Returns the directory path used to look for zonefiles (either system or built-in).
requirements: Do not free or modify the returned string.

functions.name: icaltimezone_set_zone_directory
functions.description: Sets the directory to search for zonefiles (system or built-in).
requirements: path should be a valid directory path where zonefiles can be found.

functions.name: icaltimezone_free_zone_directory
functions.description: Frees memory associated with the configured zonefile directory path.
requirements: Should be called when the custom zone directory string is no longer needed (ownership managed by the library).

functions.name: icaltimezone_set_builtin_tzdata
functions.description: Enables or disables use of built-in timezone data files.
requirements: set == true enables built-in tzdata; set == false disables it.
Callers should set this before operations that depend on timezone data source selection.

functions.name: icaltimezone_get_builtin_tzdata
functions.description: Returns whether the library is configured to use built-in timezone data files.

functions.name: icaltimezone_dump_changes
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT bool icaltimezone_dump_changes(icaltimezone *zone, int max_year, FILE *fp);
functions.description: Writes a list of timezone changes for the given timezone to the provided FILE up to max_year, in a format compatible with 'vzic --dump-changes' verification. Returns true on success.
requirements: zone must be a valid icaltimezone pointer.
fp must be a valid, writable FILE*; the function writes text in the format: "Zone-Name\tDate\tTime\tUTC-Offset" with Date/Time in UTC and offset as seconds to add to UTC.
max_year sets an upper bound on the year of reported changes; callers should ensure it is reasonable for their use.

functions.name: icaltriggertype_from_seconds
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT struct icaltriggertype icaltriggertype_from_seconds(const int reltime);
functions.description: Constructs an icaltriggertype from a relative offset given in seconds. Typical usage is to build a trigger (e.g., relative to an event start) from an integer offset. Exact interpretation of sign and range is not documented here; details unknown.
requirements: reltime must be a valid int value; valid range and sign semantics are unknown
No ownership or lifetime management is required for the returned struct (it is returned by value)
Caller should treat behavior for extreme values (overflow ranges) as unspecified

functions.name: icaltriggertype_from_string
functions.description: Parses a C string to construct an icaltriggertype. Intended for creating a trigger from its textual representation. Exact accepted formats are not specified here; details unknown.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL pointer to a NUL-terminated C string
str must remain valid for the duration of the call
Accepted string syntax and locale/encoding expectations are not specified; callers should supply a standard libical trigger format

functions.name: icaltriggertype_is_null_trigger
functions.description: Returns true if the supplied icaltriggertype represents a null/empty trigger. Intended for validation or presence checks. The exact criteria for a "null" trigger are not documented here; details unknown.
requirements: tr should be properly initialized (not contain uninitialized memory) before being passed

functions.name: icaltriggertype_is_bad_trigger
functions.description: Returns true if the supplied icaltriggertype is invalid or malformed. Useful for validating triggers before use. The specific validation rules are not documented here; details unknown.
requirements: tr should be properly initialized (not contain uninitialized memory) before being passed

functions.name: icalreqstattype_from_string
functions.description: Parses a textual request-status value into an icalreqstattype struct (status code, description, and optional debug text). Use when reading a request_status property from text. Parsing rules and exact string format are not specified here; details unknown.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL pointer to a NUL-terminated C string
str must remain valid for the duration of the call
The returned struct contains pointers: desc points to a static table owned by the library and must not be freed; debug is owned by the icalvalue and must not be freed manually

functions.name: icalreqstattype_as_string
functions.description: Serializes an icalreqstattype to a textual representation. Use for emitting a request_status property value as text. Memory ownership and lifetime of the returned pointer are not documented here; details unknown.
requirements: Input struct should be properly initialized
Do not free the returned pointer unless explicitly documented elsewhere (ownership unspecified)

functions.name: icalreqstattype_as_string_r
functions.description: Serializes an icalreqstattype to a textual representation in a re-entrant form, returning a char*. Common patterns suggest a newly allocated string, but ownership details are not specified here; details unknown.
requirements: Input struct should be properly initialized
The ownership/lifetime of the returned char* is not specified; callers must consult library documentation before freeing

functions.name: ical_get_unknown_token_handling_setting
functions.description: Returns the current library setting for how unknown tokens are handled. Note: per the header comment, this currently affects parameters; extension to components and properties is a FIXME.

functions.name: ical_set_unknown_token_handling_setting
functions.description: Sets the library-wide policy for handling unknown tokens (e.g., parameters). Valid values are ICAL_ASSUME_IANA_TOKEN, ICAL_DISCARD_TOKEN, or ICAL_TREAT_AS_ERROR. Per the header comment, this currently only affects parameters.
requirements: newSetting must be one of the defined ical_unknown_token_handling enum values: ICAL_ASSUME_IANA_TOKEN, ICAL_DISCARD_TOKEN, or ICAL_TREAT_AS_ERROR
This changes a global/library-wide setting; thread-safety and concurrency guarantees are not specified

functions.name: icalvalue_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new icalvalue of the specified kind. Use to create a value object before setting/getting its contents or attaching it to components/properties. Details about initial state are not documented here; typically the value starts unset/empty for its kind.
requirements: kind must be a valid icalvalue_kind (use icalvalue_kind_is_valid to check).
The returned pointer must be freed with icalvalue_free when no longer needed.
Do not pass the returned object to other APIs until it has been properly initialized for its kind (exact initialization steps are library-dependent and not documented here).

functions.name: icalvalue_clone
functions.description: Deeply clones an icalvalue, returning a new, independent copy. Use when you need to duplicate a value without sharing internal state. Returns a pointer to the newly cloned value. Since 4.0.
requirements: old must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid icalvalue.
The returned clone must be freed with icalvalue_free.
The source value must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: icalvalue_new_from_string
functions.description: Parses an iCalendar-formatted string as the given kind and constructs a new icalvalue. Use to create a value from its textual iCalendar representation.
requirements: kind must be a valid icalvalue_kind matching the textual representation supplied.
str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string containing the value in the correct iCalendar syntax for the specified kind.
On success, the returned value must be freed with icalvalue_free.
If parsing fails, the function may return NULL; callers must check the return value before use (behavior inferred; exact failure mode not documented).

functions.name: icalvalue_free
functions.description: Frees an icalvalue previously created by this library (e.g., via icalvalue_new, icalvalue_new_from_string, icalvalue_clone). Use to release memory and resources associated with a value.
requirements: value must be either NULL or a pointer returned by this library for an icalvalue; do not free arbitrary or stack-allocated objects (acceptance of NULL is not documented; safest is to pass a valid non-NULL icalvalue).
Do not use the value after calling this function (no double-free or use-after-free).
Do not free the same value more than once.

functions.name: icalvalue_is_valid
functions.description: Returns whether the provided icalvalue is structurally and semantically valid. Use to validate a value before serialization or attaching to components/properties.
requirements: value should be a non-NULL pointer to an icalvalue (behavior on NULL is not documented).
Callers must check the boolean return to handle invalid values appropriately.

functions.name: icalvalue_as_ical_string
functions.description: Serializes an icalvalue to its iCalendar text representation and returns it as a C string. Useful for emitting property values in .ics format. The returned string is const and managed by the library (exact ownership/lifetime is not explicitly documented here).
requirements: value must be a non-NULL, valid icalvalue.
The returned pointer must not be modified by the caller.

If the function uses an internal/static buffer, the returned pointer may become invalid after subsequent library calls; callers should copy the string if needed beyond immediate use (inferred; exact lifetime not documented).
Callers should check for NULL if serialization fails (failure behavior not documented).

functions.name: icalvalue_as_ical_string_r
functions.description: Reentrant/allocated variant of serialization: converts an icalvalue to its iCalendar text and returns a newly allocated C string suitable for thread-safe use. Intended when the caller needs ownership of the string.
requirements: value must be a non-NULL, valid icalvalue.

The returned string is heap-allocated; the caller is responsible for freeing it (exact deallocation routine is not specified here; typically a standard free or a library-specific free may be required—consult libical memory management).
Callers should check for NULL to detect serialization/allocation failure.

functions.name: icalvalue_isa
functions.description: Returns the kind (type tag) of the given icalvalue. Use to query the runtime type before performing kind-specific operations.
requirements: value should be a non-NULL pointer to an icalvalue (behavior on NULL is not documented).
Callers must handle the case where an unknown/invalid kind may be returned if the value is invalid (inferred from presence of kind validation APIs).

functions.name: icalvalue_isa_value
functions.description: Returns whether the supplied pointer refers to an icalvalue object. Useful for dynamic type checks in C APIs that pass generic pointers.
requirements: The argument may be any pointer; it need not be non-NULL (exact behavior on NULL is not documented).
No ownership is transferred; this function does not modify or free the argument.

functions.name: icalvalue_compare
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT icalparameter_xliccomparetype icalvalue_compare(const icalvalue *a, const icalvalue *b);
functions.description: Compares two icalvalues and returns an icalparameter_xliccomparetype indicating the relationship. Returns ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_NOTEQUAL if the values do not have the same type. Returns ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_NONE if the values’ type is unknown or if one of the values is NULL.
requirements: a and b may be NULL; if either is NULL, the function returns ICAL_XLICCOMPARETYPE_NONE (per documentation).
a and b should generally be valid icalvalues of the same kind to obtain meaningful comparison results.
Callers must handle all possible enum results, including NOTEQUAL and NONE.

functions.name: icalvalue_string_to_kind
functions.description: Converts a textual kind name to its icalvalue_kind enumeration. Use to map strings (e.g., from user input or files) to the library’s kind identifiers.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string containing a kind name recognized by libical.
Callers must handle the case where the returned kind indicates an unknown/invalid value if the string is not recognized (exact sentinel not specified here).

functions.name: icalvalue_kind_to_string
functions.description: Converts an icalvalue_kind enumeration to its canonical string representation.
requirements: kind should be a valid icalvalue_kind; callers may receive a string for unknown kinds depending on implementation (not documented).
The returned pointer is managed by the library and must not be modified or freed by the caller.

functions.name: icalvalue_kind_is_valid
functions.description: Checks whether the provided icalvalue_kind value is a valid/recognized kind.
requirements: kind may be any icalvalue_kind value; callers should use the boolean result to gate further operations.

functions.name: icalvalue_encode_ical_string
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT bool icalvalue_encode_ical_string(const char *szText,                                                       char *szEncText, int MaxBufferLen);
functions.description: Encodes a character string into iCalendar format, escaping certain characters as required by the specification, and writes the result into the provided destination buffer.
requirements: szText must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated source string.
szEncText must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer with capacity of at least MaxBufferLen bytes.
MaxBufferLen must be a positive integer specifying the size, in bytes, of szEncText.

The destination buffer must be large enough to hold the fully encoded string including the terminating NUL; on insufficient space the function may return false (exact failure behavior not fully documented).
Source and destination buffers must not overlap (inferred from typical C encoding routines).
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect failure.

functions.name: icalvalue_decode_ical_string
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICAL_EXPORT bool icalvalue_decode_ical_string(const char *szText,                                                       char *szDecText, int nMaxBufferLen);
functions.description: Decodes a string previously encoded for iCalendar (unescapes characters) and writes the original text into the provided destination buffer.
requirements: szText must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated encoded source string.
szDecText must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer with capacity of at least nMaxBufferLen bytes.
nMaxBufferLen must be a positive integer specifying the size, in bytes, of szDecText.

The destination buffer must be large enough to hold the fully decoded string including the terminating NUL; on insufficient space the function may return false (exact failure behavior not fully documented).
Source and destination buffers must not overlap (inferred from typical C decoding routines).
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect failure.

functions.name: icalpvl_new_element
functions.signature: icalpvl_elem icalpvl_new_element(void *d, icalpvl_elem next, icalpvl_elem prior);
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new list element (node) initialized with user data d and links to adjacent elements next and prior. Intended for internal/advanced manipulation of the pvl list structure.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
The next and prior pointers, if non-NULL, should refer to elements from the same pvl list to avoid corrupting list structure.
The data pointer d is stored as-is; its lifetime/ownership is managed by the caller unless otherwise documented by higher-level APIs.
Do not mix icalpvl_elem objects from different lists.

functions.name: icalpvl_newlist
functions.description: Creates and returns an empty pvl list capable of storing void* items.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
Caller must eventually release the list with icalpvl_free (and/or clear it as appropriate).
The returned list must be used only with icalpvl_* functions operating on icalpvl_list.

functions.name: icalpvl_free
functions.description: Releases resources associated with the list l. Exact ownership of stored data pointers is not specified here; see library behavior elsewhere. Typically frees internal structures and the list container.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
The list l must have been created by icalpvl_newlist.
After calling, l must not be used.

Ownership/lifetime of user data pointers contained in the list is unspecified by this header; do not assume they are freed unless previously cleared via icalpvl_clear (which states it de-allocates all data).

functions.name: icalpvl_unshift
functions.description: Inserts a new element containing data d at the head of list l.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
d is stored as a raw pointer; caller is responsible for its lifetime unless otherwise handled by list-clear semantics.

functions.name: icalpvl_shift
functions.description: Removes and returns the data pointer stored in the head element of list l.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
Caller assumes ownership/responsibility for the returned data pointer.
Behavior when the list is empty is not specified here; handle a possible NULL return.

functions.name: icalpvl_head
functions.description: Returns the first element (node) in list l without removing it.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
May return NULL if the list is empty.

functions.name: icalpvl_push
functions.description: Appends a new element containing data d to the tail of list l.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
d is stored as a raw pointer; caller manages its lifetime unless otherwise handled by list-clear semantics.

functions.name: icalpvl_pop
functions.description: Removes and returns the data pointer stored in the tail element of list l.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
Caller assumes ownership/responsibility for the returned data pointer.
Behavior when the list is empty is not specified here; handle a possible NULL return.

functions.name: icalpvl_tail
functions.description: Returns the last element (node) in list l without removing it.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
May return NULL if the list is empty.

functions.name: icalpvl_insert_ordered
functions.signature: void icalpvl_insert_ordered(icalpvl_list l, icalpvl_comparef f, void *d);
functions.description: Inserts data d into list l at the position determined by comparator f, maintaining an order according to f. The comparator receives two data pointers and should order them.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
f must be a valid function pointer of type int (*)(void*, void*); it must be consistent with the data stored in l.
d is stored as-is; caller manages its lifetime unless otherwise handled by list-clear semantics.
Comparator semantics (return value meaning) are not specified here; it should provide a strict weak ordering suitable for insertion.

functions.name: icalpvl_insert_after
functions.signature: void icalpvl_insert_after(icalpvl_list l, icalpvl_elem p, void *d);
functions.description: Inserts a new element with data d into list l immediately after element p.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
p must be a valid element belonging to l.
d is stored as a raw pointer; caller manages its lifetime unless otherwise handled by list-clear semantics.

functions.name: icalpvl_insert_before
functions.signature: void icalpvl_insert_before(icalpvl_list l, icalpvl_elem p, void *d);
functions.description: Inserts a new element with data d into list l immediately before element p.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
p must be a valid element belonging to l.
d is stored as a raw pointer; caller manages its lifetime unless otherwise handled by list-clear semantics.

functions.name: icalpvl_remove
functions.description: Unlinks element e from list l and returns its stored data pointer without deallocating it.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
e must be a valid element currently contained in l.
Caller becomes responsible for the returned data pointer.
Behavior when e is NULL or not in l is not specified; callers should avoid such cases.

functions.name: icalpvl_clear
functions.description: Removes all elements from list l and de-allocates all data. After this call, the list is empty and previously stored data pointers must not be used.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
All data stored in the list will be de-allocated; callers must not access or free those pointers after this call.

functions.name: icalpvl_count
functions.description: Returns the number of elements in list l.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.

functions.name: icalpvl_next
functions.description: Returns the next element following e in the list, or NULL if none.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
e must be a valid element obtained from an icalpvl_list.

functions.name: icalpvl_prior
functions.description: Returns the previous element before e in the list, or NULL if none.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
e must be a valid element obtained from an icalpvl_list.

functions.name: icalpvl_data
functions.description: Returns the data pointer stored in element e.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
e must be a valid element obtained from an icalpvl_list.
Returned pointer is the stored payload; its lifetime is managed by the list/caller as per usage of other functions (e.g., icalpvl_clear de-allocates all data).

functions.name: icalpvl_find
functions.signature: icalpvl_elem icalpvl_find(icalpvl_list l, icalpvl_findf f, void *v);
functions.description: Finds and returns the first element in list l for which predicate f returns true when called as f(a, v), where a is the list element (as per typedef comment).
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
f must be a valid function pointer of type int (*)(void*, void*). The first argument corresponds to the list element (see header comment), the second is the user-supplied value v.
Predicate must be safe to call for each element in the list.
May return NULL if no element matches.

functions.name: icalpvl_find_next
functions.signature: icalpvl_elem icalpvl_find_next(icalpvl_list l, icalpvl_findf f, void *v);
functions.description: Continues a search in list l and returns the next element for which predicate f returns true when called as f(a, v). Typically used after icalpvl_find to iterate matches.
requirements: This is an internal-only API; behavior and ABI may change without notice.
l must be a valid list created by icalpvl_newlist.
f must be a valid function pointer of type int (*)(void*, void*). The first argument corresponds to the list element (see header comment), the second is the user-supplied value v.

functions.name: icalspanlist_free
functions.description: Frees a spanlist and its resources.
requirements: sl may be NULL (behavior if NULL not documented, unknown).
After calling, sl must not be used again.

functions.name: icalspanlist_next_free_time
functions.signature: struct icalperiodtype icalspanlist_next_free_time(icalspanlist *sl, struct icaltimetype t);
functions.description: Finds and returns the next free time period in the spanlist starting at time t.
requirements: sl must be a valid icalspanlist.
t must be a valid icaltimetype.

functions.name: icalspanlist_dump
functions.description: Debug helper that prints the spanlist to STDOUT.
requirements: sl should be a valid icalspanlist.
Output is to STDOUT; ensure appropriate environment.

functions.name: icalspanlist_as_vfreebusy
functions.description: Builds and returns a VFREEBUSY component from the spanlist. The start time maps to DTSTART and end time to DTEND. Each busy span becomes a FREEBUSY entry. Attendee is required; organizer is optional.
requirements: sl must be a valid icalspanlist created by icalspanlist_new.
attendee must be a non-NULL string in the form "MAILTO:user@domain" (as documented).
organizer may be NULL or a string in the form "MAILTO:user@domain" (as documented).
Returns NULL on failure (implied).

functions.name: icalspanlist_as_freebusy_matrix
functions.description: Returns an hour-by-hour (or specified slice) array of busy counts over the spanlist period. The final array entry is -1. If the spanlist start/end don't align to delta_t boundaries, results may be unexpected. Calculation subtracts one second from end times to handle inclusivity.
requirements: spanlist must be a valid icalspanlist.
delta_t is the time slice in seconds; default is 3600 if not otherwise specified (callers should provide a positive integer).
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned int array (ownership implied; not explicitly documented).

functions.name: icalspanlist_from_vfreebusy
functions.description: Constructs and returns an icalspanlist from the VFREEBUSY component contained in the given icalcomponent, or NULL if no VFREEBUSY section exists.
requirements: comp must be a valid icalcomponent containing a VFREEBUSY section.
Returns NULL if no VFREEBUSY section found.

functions.name: icalmessage_new_accept_reply
functions.signature: icalcomponent *icalmessage_new_accept_reply(const icalcomponent *c, const char *user, const char *msg);
functions.description: Creates an iTIP/iMIP accept reply component responding to the given component on behalf of user, optionally including a message.
requirements: c must be a valid icalcomponent representing the original request/invitation.
user must be a valid identifier string for the responding user.
msg may be NULL or a null-terminated string.

functions.name: icalmessage_new_decline_reply
functions.signature: icalcomponent *icalmessage_new_decline_reply(const icalcomponent *c, const char *user, const char *msg);
functions.description: Creates a decline reply component responding to the given component on behalf of user, optionally including a message.
requirements: c must be a valid icalcomponent representing the original request/invitation.
user must be a valid identifier string for the responding user.
msg may be NULL or a null-terminated string.

functions.name: icalmessage_new_counterpropose_reply
functions.signature: icalcomponent *icalmessage_new_counterpropose_reply(const icalcomponent *oldc, const icalcomponent *newc, const char *user, const char *msg);
functions.description: Creates a counterproposal reply based on the original component and a new proposed component, for the given user, with an optional message.
requirements: oldc must be a valid icalcomponent representing the original proposal.
newc must be a valid icalcomponent representing the counterproposal.
user must be a valid identifier string for the responding user.
msg may be NULL or a null-terminated string.

functions.name: icalmessage_new_delegate_reply
functions.signature: icalcomponent *icalmessage_new_delegate_reply(const icalcomponent *c, const char *user, const char *delegatee, const char *msg);
functions.description: Creates a delegation reply component for the given user and delegatee, optionally including a message.
requirements: c must be a valid icalcomponent representing the original request/invitation.
user must be a valid identifier string for the delegating user.
delegatee must be a valid identifier string for the delegatee.
msg may be NULL or a null-terminated string.

functions.name: icalmessage_new_error_reply
functions.signature: icalcomponent *icalmessage_new_error_reply(const icalcomponent *c, const char *user, const char *msg, const char *debug, icalrequeststatus code);
functions.description: Creates an error reply component describing an error condition for the given user, with an optional message and debug text, and a required iTIP request status code.
requirements: c must be a valid icalcomponent related to the error context.
user must be a valid identifier string for the reporting user.
msg may be NULL or a null-terminated string.
debug may be NULL or a null-terminated string.
code must be a valid icalrequeststatus value.

functions.name: icalcalendar_new
functions.description: Create a new calendar object backed by a directory-based store. Expected usage: pass a filesystem path to a directory that will contain the calendar’s incoming, booked, properties, and free/busy sets; the function returns an opaque icalcalendar handle to be used with other icalcalendar_* APIs. Notes: ownership of the returned pointer is transferred to the caller; free it with icalcalendar_free when no longer needed. Detailed behavior on invalid paths or permissions is not specified in this header.
requirements: dir must be a valid NUL-terminated C string
The path referenced by dir is expected to denote a directory suitable for calendar storage (exact requirements unknown)
Caller assumes ownership of the returned icalcalendar* and must release it with icalcalendar_free
Do not use the returned pointer after it is freed

functions.name: icalcalendar_free
functions.description: Destroy and release all resources associated with a calendar created by icalcalendar_new. Expected usage: call exactly once for each successful icalcalendar_new to avoid leaks. Notes: behavior on NULL is not specified in this header; avoid passing NULL unless documented elsewhere.
requirements: calendar must be a valid pointer previously returned by icalcalendar_new
Call at most once per calendar instance
Do not use calendar or any derived resources (e.g., icalset pointers returned by getters) after this call

functions.name: icalcalendar_lock
functions.description: Acquire a lock on the calendar’s backing store to synchronize access. Expected usage: call before modifying or enumerating calendar data that must be protected; pair with icalcalendar_unlock. Notes: returns an int status; specific return codes are not specified here.
requirements: calendar must be a valid, initialized calendar pointer
Should be paired with a matching icalcalendar_unlock when a lock is successfully acquired
Only call from contexts that respect the library’s locking discipline; do not recursively lock unless the implementation is known to allow it (capability unknown)
Check the return value to determine success or failure (exact semantics unknown)

functions.name: icalcalendar_unlock
functions.description: Release a previously acquired lock on the calendar’s backing store. Expected usage: call after a successful icalcalendar_lock to relinquish exclusive access. Notes: returns an int status; specific return codes are not specified here.
requirements: calendar must be a valid, initialized calendar pointer
Only call after a successful icalcalendar_lock by the same caller/context
Check the return value to determine success or failure (exact semantics unknown)

functions.name: icalcalendar_islocked
functions.description: Query whether the calendar is currently locked. Expected usage: use to test lock state prior to attempting operations that require locking. Notes: returns an int; exact convention (e.g., 0/1) is not specified in this header.
requirements: calendar must be a valid, initialized calendar pointer
Caller must interpret the int return according to library documentation (exact mapping unknown)

functions.name: icalcalendar_ownlock
functions.description: Determine whether the current caller/context owns the calendar’s lock. Expected usage: check ownership before performing operations that require the caller to hold the lock, or before unlocking. Notes: returns an int; exact convention (e.g., 0/1) is not specified in this header.
requirements: calendar must be a valid, initialized calendar pointer
Only meaningful if locking is in use; semantics depend on the implementation’s notion of lock ownership (details unknown)
Caller must interpret the int return according to library documentation (exact mapping unknown)

functions.name: icalcalendar_get_booked
functions.description: Access the set of booked components in the calendar. Expected usage: obtain an icalset handle for reading and/or modifying booked items. Notes: ownership of the returned icalset is not stated here; treat it as a borrowed reference tied to the calendar unless documented otherwise.
requirements: calendar must be a valid, initialized calendar pointer
Do not use the returned icalset after the parent calendar is freed
Do not free the returned icalset unless the broader API explicitly documents that the caller owns it (ownership unknown)

functions.name: icalcalendar_get_incoming
functions.description: Access the set of incoming components in the calendar. Expected usage: obtain an icalset handle for reading and/or processing incoming items. Notes: ownership of the returned icalset is not stated here; treat it as a borrowed reference tied to the calendar unless documented otherwise.
requirements: calendar must be a valid, initialized calendar pointer
Do not use the returned icalset after the parent calendar is freed
Do not free the returned icalset unless the broader API explicitly documents that the caller owns it (ownership unknown)

functions.name: icalcalendar_get_properties
functions.description: Access the set of calendar properties. Expected usage: obtain an icalset handle to inspect or modify calendar-level properties. Notes: ownership of the returned icalset is not stated here; treat it as a borrowed reference tied to the calendar unless documented otherwise.
requirements: calendar must be a valid, initialized calendar pointer
Do not use the returned icalset after the parent calendar is freed
Do not free the returned icalset unless the broader API explicitly documents that the caller owns it (ownership unknown)

functions.name: icalcalendar_get_freebusy
functions.description: Access the free/busy set associated with the calendar. Expected usage: obtain an icalset handle to query or update free/busy information. Notes: ownership of the returned icalset is not stated here; treat it as a borrowed reference tied to the calendar unless documented otherwise.
requirements: calendar must be a valid, initialized calendar pointer
Do not use the returned icalset after the parent calendar is freed
Do not free the returned icalset unless the broader API explicitly documents that the caller owns it (ownership unknown)

functions.name: icalclassify
functions.signature: LIBICAL_ICALSS_EXPORT icalproperty_xlicclass icalclassify(icalcomponent *c, icalcomponent *match, const char *user);
functions.description: Classifies the given iCalendar component, likely returning an icalproperty_xlicclass value that indicates the classification or handling of the component in relation to a potential matching component and a user identity. Typical usage would be to call this with a fully-initialized icalcomponent to determine how it should be treated (e.g., scheduling context), possibly relative to another component and the specified user. Detailed behavior, classification criteria, and ownership semantics are not documented in this header and remain unknown.
requirements: c must point to a valid, initialized icalcomponent.
If provided, match must point to a valid, initialized icalcomponent; its specific role is not documented in this header.
user must be a valid, null-terminated C string if not NULL; how it is used is not documented in this header.
Caller should not pass NULL pointers unless the implementation explicitly allows them; allowances are not specified here.
Return value is an icalproperty_xlicclass enum; exact mapping of values and error indicators (if any) are not specified in this header.

functions.name: icalclassify_find_overlaps
functions.description: Searches the given icalset for components that overlap with the time span of the provided component and returns an icalcomponent representing an overlap (exact semantics unknown). Expected usage is to supply a populated set and a component (e.g., VEVENT) and obtain an overlapping component if one exists. The precise selection rules, whether multiple overlaps are possible, and ownership/iteration semantics are not documented in this header and remain unknown.
requirements: set must point to a valid, initialized icalset containing components to search.
comp must point to a valid, initialized icalcomponent whose time range (e.g., DTSTART/DTEND) can be evaluated; required properties are not specified here.
Return may be NULL or a valid icalcomponent pointer; ownership and lifetime of the returned pointer are not specified in this header.
Behavior for recurring components, time zones, and boundary inclusivity are not specified in this header.

functions.name: icalcluster_new
functions.description: Creates a new opaque icalcluster keyed by the provided key and initialized with the given icalcomponent payload. Intended as a constructor for a key/value cluster object. Notes: the header’s TODO mentions deep-copy semantics may not always be used; ownership and copy semantics of key and data are therefore not fully specified by this header.
requirements: key should point to a valid, NUL-terminated C string (non-NULL recommended).
data should be a valid pointer to an icalcomponent compatible with clustering (non-NULL recommended).
Ownership and lifetime of key and data after the call are not documented; callers should not assume either deep copy or transfer of ownership without consulting implementation/documentation.
The returned icalcluster* must be freed with icalcluster_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: icalcluster_clone
functions.description: Performs a deep clone of an existing icalcluster and returns a new icalcluster with duplicated content. Useful for copying clusters without sharing internal state. Introduced in libical 4.0.
requirements: old must point to a valid icalcluster.
The returned icalcluster* is a new allocation and must be freed with icalcluster_free.
Cloning semantics are documented as deep; internal components and state are duplicated rather than shared, subject to any library-defined exceptions.

functions.name: icalcluster_free
functions.description: Destroys and releases all resources associated with the given icalcluster. After this call, the pointer must not be used.
requirements: cluster must be a pointer previously returned by icalcluster_new or icalcluster_clone (or otherwise properly constructed by the library).
Do not use cluster after freeing it (dangling pointer).
Do not call icalcluster_free more than once on the same object (no double-free).

functions.name: icalcluster_key
functions.description: Returns the key string associated with the cluster. The returned pointer is to an internal string; callers should treat it as read-only.
requirements: cluster must point to a valid icalcluster.
The returned const char* should be treated as read-only; do not modify or free it.
Lifetime/ownership of the returned string is tied to the cluster; its validity after cluster modification is not documented.

functions.name: icalcluster_is_changed
functions.description: Reports whether the cluster is marked as changed since the last commit/reset. Intended to track modification state of the cluster.
requirements: cluster must point to a valid icalcluster.
Returned int is a boolean-like indicator (nonzero/zero); exact semantics beyond change tracking are not detailed in this header.

functions.name: icalcluster_mark
functions.description: Marks the cluster as changed. Typically used to indicate that the cluster’s contents or metadata has been modified since the last commit/reset.
requirements: cluster must point to a valid icalcluster.

Intended to be called when the caller knows the cluster was modified; exact interaction with icalcluster_is_changed/icalcluster_commit follows typical change-tracking patterns but is not fully specified.

functions.name: icalcluster_commit
functions.description: Commits or clears the cluster’s change state. This commonly resets the change marker (e.g., after persisting updates), though exact semantics are not specified in the header.
requirements: cluster must point to a valid icalcluster.
Call when you want to acknowledge/clear pending changes; precise persistence side-effects are not documented here.

functions.name: icalcluster_get_component
functions.description: Returns the primary icalcomponent stored in the cluster (the cluster’s underlying component tree).
requirements: cluster must point to a valid icalcluster.
The returned icalcomponent pointer is owned by the cluster; do not free it unless ownership transfer is specifically documented elsewhere (not specified here).

functions.name: icalcluster_count_components
functions.description: Counts and returns the number of subcomponents of the specified kind contained within the cluster’s component.
requirements: cluster must point to a valid icalcluster.
kind must be a valid icalcomponent_kind value.
Return value is a non-negative count on success; specific error signaling (e.g., negative values) is not documented in this header.

functions.name: icalcluster_add_component
functions.description: Adds the specified child icalcomponent to the cluster’s component tree. Returns an icalerrorenum indicating success or the specific error.
requirements: cluster must point to a valid icalcluster.
child must point to a valid icalcomponent expected/allowed by the cluster’s component hierarchy.
Caller must check the returned icalerrorenum and handle errors appropriately.
Ownership/lifetime of child after a successful add is not explicitly documented; typical library patterns imply it may become owned by the cluster, but this header does not guarantee it.

functions.name: icalcluster_remove_component
functions.description: Removes the specified child icalcomponent from the cluster’s component tree. Returns an icalerrorenum indicating success or error.
requirements: cluster must point to a valid icalcluster.
child must point to a valid icalcomponent that is currently part of the cluster’s component tree.
Caller must check and handle the returned icalerrorenum for error conditions.
Ownership of child after removal is not specified here; callers should not assume automatic free or retained ownership without consulting implementation/documentation.

functions.name: icalcluster_get_current_component
functions.description: Returns the current component in the cluster’s internal iteration state. Used together with get_first/get_next to iterate subcomponents.
requirements: cluster must point to a valid icalcluster.
Intended to be used after icalcluster_get_first_component has initialized iteration; behavior when no iteration is active is not documented.

functions.name: icalcluster_get_first_component
functions.description: Initializes iteration and returns the first component in the cluster’s component sequence.
requirements: cluster must point to a valid icalcluster.
Typically call this to begin iteration, then repeatedly call icalcluster_get_next_component until it returns NULL; exact ordering and filtering rules are not specified here.

functions.name: icalcluster_get_next_component
functions.description: Advances the internal iterator and returns the next component in the cluster’s component sequence, or NULL when no more components remain.
requirements: cluster must point to a valid icalcluster.
Should be called after icalcluster_get_first_component and repeated until NULL is returned.
The returned component is owned by the cluster; do not free it unless ownership transfer is documented elsewhere.

functions.name: icaldirset_new
functions.description: Creates a new directory-backed icalset store rooted at the given directory path, opened for general use (read/write mode is implied by implementation). Intended as the primary constructor for an icaldirset.
requirements: dir must be a valid, accessible filesystem directory path.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect errors.
The resulting icalset must be freed with icaldirset_free().
Thread-safety is unknown; do not share the returned icalset across threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: icaldirset_new_reader
functions.description: Creates a new icaldirset store opened in reader mode (read-only). Use when only reading components from the directory-backed store.
requirements: dir must be a valid, accessible filesystem directory path.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect errors.
The resulting icalset must be freed with icaldirset_free().
Modifying functions (add/remove/modify/commit/mark) should not be used on a reader; behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: icaldirset_new_writer
functions.description: Creates a new icaldirset store opened in writer mode (writable). Use when adding/removing/modifying components.
requirements: dir must be a valid, accessible filesystem directory path; must be writable by the process.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect errors.
The resulting icalset must be freed with icaldirset_free().

functions.name: icaldirset_init
functions.description: Initializes an existing icalset object as a directory-backed set rooted at dir, using optional implementation-specific options. Returns the initialized set.
requirements: set must be a valid icalset pointer created by compatible allocation code (exact creation mechanism is not specified).
dir must be a valid, accessible filesystem directory path.
options_in may be NULL; when provided, it is expected to point to an icaldirset_options structure (inferred from header), but exact interpretation is implementation-defined.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect initialization failure.

functions.name: icaldirset_free
functions.description: Releases all resources associated with a directory-backed icalset. If the set has pending changes and has been marked, changes may be written upon free (per implementation).
requirements: set may be NULL (behavior unspecified in header); passing a valid set is required to actually free resources.
After calling, the set pointer must not be used again.
If write-back is needed immediately, call icaldirset_commit() prior to freeing; otherwise rely on implementation’s flush-on-free behavior only if acceptable.

functions.name: icaldirset_path
functions.description: Returns the filesystem path of the directory backing the given icaldirset.
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset.
Returned pointer is owned by the set; do not free it and expect it to remain valid while the set lives.
Caller should handle NULL return if the path is unavailable.

functions.name: icaldirset_mark
functions.description: Marks the current cluster/store as changed so it will be written to disk when freed. Use icaldirset_commit() to write immediately.
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset.
Marking does not itself persist changes; caller should later call icaldirset_commit() or rely on write-on-free semantics.

functions.name: icaldirset_commit
functions.description: Immediately writes any pending changes for the directory-backed icalset to disk.
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset opened with permissions sufficient to write.
Caller must check the returned icalerrorenum for success/failure and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: icaldirset_add_component
functions.description: Adds a component to the store. Assumes a VCALENDAR top-level with an inner VEVENT/VTODO/VJOURNAL, and that the inner component has a DTSTAMP property. The store will generate UIDs for stored objects that lack one.
requirements: set must be a valid, writable icaldirset.
comp must not be NULL.
comp is expected to be a VCALENDAR containing one inner component of type VEVENT, VTODO, or VJOURNAL.
The inner component must have a DTSTAMP property (explicitly stated).
Caller must check the returned icalerrorenum and handle errors.

functions.name: icaldirset_remove_component
functions.description: Removes the specified component from the store.
requirements: set must be a valid, writable icaldirset.
comp must not be NULL and should refer to a component present in the set.
Caller must check the returned icalerrorenum and handle errors.

functions.name: icaldirset_count_components
functions.description: Counts the number of components of the specified kind in the store.
requirements: store must be a valid icaldirset.
kind must be a valid icalcomponent_kind value.
Caller should handle negative values only if specified by implementation; header does not define error signaling besides returning an int (treat result < 0 as unknown/error).

functions.name: icaldirset_select
functions.description: Applies a selection gauge to the set. Subsequent iteration functions return only components that pass the gauge.
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset.
gauge may be NULL only if the intent is to clear selection via icaldirset_clear(); behavior of passing NULL here is not specified in header.
Caller must check the returned icalerrorenum and handle errors.

functions.name: icaldirset_clear
functions.description: Clears any previously set gauge so that iteration returns all components.
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset.

functions.name: icaldirset_fetch
functions.description: Fetches a component by UID and kind from the store.
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset.
uid must be a non-NULL string identifying the target component.
kind must be a valid icalcomponent_kind for the sought component.
Caller must handle NULL return when no matching component exists.

functions.name: icaldirset_has_uid
functions.description: Checks whether a component with the given UID exists in the set.
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset.
uid must be a non-NULL string.
Return value semantics are not detailed; treat 0 as not found and non-zero as found (inferred by common C conventions).

functions.name: icaldirset_fetch_match
functions.description: Fetches a component from the store that matches the given component c (match criteria are implementation-defined).
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset.
c must be a non-NULL pointer to an icalcomponent to use as a matching template.
Caller must handle NULL return when no matching component exists.
Exact matching rules are unknown; rely on implementation.

functions.name: icaldirset_modify
functions.description: Modifies components according to the CAP MODIFY method. Operates on currently selected components (i.e., those passing the active gauge).
requirements: set must be a valid, writable icaldirset.
oldcomp and newcomp must be non-NULL icalcomponents.
A selection gauge, if set, restricts which components are subject to modification.
Caller must check the returned icalerrorenum and handle errors.

functions.name: icaldirset_get_current_component
functions.description: Returns the current component in an internal iteration context, considering any active gauge.
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset.
Must be called within a valid iteration context established by get_first/get_next or other internal iteration; otherwise return may be NULL or unspecified.
Caller must handle NULL return.

functions.name: icaldirset_get_first_component
functions.description: Starts internal iteration and returns the first component in the set that passes the current gauge (if any).
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset.
Caller must handle NULL return when the set is empty or no component passes the gauge.
Subsequent calls to icaldirset_get_next_component() continue the iteration.

functions.name: icaldirset_get_next_component
functions.description: Continues internal iteration, returning the next component that passes the current gauge (if any).
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset.
Must be preceded by icaldirset_get_first_component() to initialize iteration.
Caller must handle NULL return on end-of-iteration.

functions.name: icaldirset_begin_component
functions.signature: icalsetiter icaldirset_begin_component(icalset *set, icalcomponent_kind kind, icalgauge *gauge, const char *tzid);
functions.description: Begins an external, thread-safe iteration over components of the given kind, optionally filtered by a gauge and time zone identifier.
requirements: set must be a valid icaldirset.
kind must be a valid icalcomponent_kind.
gauge may be NULL to iterate all matching kind; otherwise it filters results.
tzid may be NULL or a valid time zone ID string as required by implementation.
The returned icalsetiter must be passed to icaldirsetiter_to_next/prior for traversal and used only with the originating set.

functions.name: icaldirsetiter_to_next
functions.description: Advances the given external iterator to the next component and returns it.
requirements: set must be the same icaldirset used to create the iterator.
i must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid icalsetiter obtained from icaldirset_begin_component().
Caller must handle NULL return on end-of-iteration or error.

functions.name: icaldirsetiter_to_prior
functions.description: Moves the given external iterator to the prior component and returns it.
requirements: set must be the same icaldirset used to create the iterator.
i must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid icalsetiter obtained from icaldirset_begin_component().
Caller must handle NULL return when there is no prior component or on error.

functions.name: icalfileset_new
functions.description: Creates a new icalfileset-based icalset associated with the file or directory at path. Intended as a general constructor that opens/initializes the set for subsequent operations (iterating, adding/removing components, etc.). Exact open mode is unspecified here.
requirements: path must be a valid filesystem path string (non-null).
The returned icalset must be freed with icalfileset_free().
Caller should treat the returned pointer as an icalfileset-backed icalset.

functions.name: icalfileset_new_reader
functions.description: Creates an icalfileset opened for reading from the given path. Use when only reading/querying components.
requirements: path must be a valid filesystem path string (non-null).
The returned icalset must be freed with icalfileset_free().

functions.name: icalfileset_new_writer
functions.description: Creates an icalfileset opened for writing to the given path. Use when adding/modifying/removing components and persisting changes.
requirements: path must be a valid filesystem path string (non-null).
The returned icalset must be freed with icalfileset_free().
Caller should ensure the path is writable according to process permissions (inferred from function name).

functions.name: icalfileset_init
functions.description: Initializes an existing icalset as an icalfileset bound to path, optionally using implementation-specific options via options_in (e.g., icalfileset_options). Use when constructing via a generic icalset_new() path and providing options.
requirements: set must be a valid, allocated icalset pointer intended for icalfileset initialization.
path must be a valid filesystem path string (non-null).
options_in may be NULL or a pointer to an icalfileset_options structure (based on naming), but exact expectations are unknown from this header.
On success, the resulting icalset should later be freed with icalfileset_free().

functions.name: icalfileset_produce_icalcluster
functions.description: Builds and returns an icalcluster loaded from the content at path. Useful for creating a cluster representation of the file’s data without creating an icalset.
requirements: path must be a valid filesystem path string (non-null).
The returned icalcluster must be freed by the caller using the appropriate libical cluster free routine (not specified in this header).

functions.name: icalfileset_free
functions.description: Frees an icalfileset-backed icalset and any associated resources. Writes may be performed if previously marked/committed behavior requires it.
requirements: set must be a valid icalset returned by an icalfileset_* constructor/init and not previously freed.
After this call, set must not be used.

functions.name: icalfileset_path
functions.description: Returns the filesystem path associated with the given icalfileset.
requirements: set must be a valid icalfileset-backed icalset.
The returned pointer is owned by the icalfileset; its lifetime is tied to the set (do not free).

functions.name: icalfileset_mark
functions.description: Marks the underlying cluster as changed so it will be written to disk when freed. Use to defer writes until destruction, unless icalfileset_commit() is used for immediate persistence.

unharnessable_functions.name: icalerror_crash_here

unharnessable_functions.name: icalparser_parse
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid icalparser_line_gen_func callback and matching opaque data, which cannot be safely provided without defining new functions under the harness constraints.

unharnessable_functions.name: icalparser_get_line
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on a caller-supplied icalparser_line_gen_func and opaque data semantics; invoking it without a proper generator risks undefined behavior under the harness constraints.

unharnessable_functions.name: icalparser_string_line_generator
unharnessable_functions.reason: Its behavior depends on an opaque data contract and a caller-managed output buffer; without defining compatible helper logic, it cannot be meaningfully exercised in this harness.

unharnessable_functions.name: icalproperty_add_parameters
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires constructing a valid va_list and passing an internal icalproperty_impl pointer, which cannot be safely generated under this fuzzer model.

unharnessable_functions.name: icalpvl_new_element
unharnessable_functions.reason: The function returns an opaque icalpvl_elem with no public deallocator or way to attach it to a list, making its lifetime unmanageable under the fuzzer model and leading to unavoidable leaks.

unharnessable_functions.name: icalset_register_class
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires constructing a custom icalset implementation with a populated vtable, which is not safely generatable under the fuzzer model.

unharnessable_functions.name: icalset_new_dir
unharnessable_functions.reason: Needs a valid directory path; the fuzzer runtime only provides file paths and cannot reliably create directories within constraints.

unharnessable_functions.name: icalfileset_init

unharnessable_functions.name: icaldirset_init

unharnessable_functions.name: icalset_register_class

unharnessable_functions.name: Parse_MIME_FromFile

unharnessable_functions.name: writeMemVObject

data_types.description: Text formatted per RFC 5545 duration syntax, e.g., PnW, PnDTnHnMnS, optionally with a leading + or -. Examples: PT5M, -P2DT3H, P1W.

Text formatted per RFC 5545 PERIOD value: either <START>/<END> where both are date-time strings, or <START>/<DURATION> where duration is an RFC 5545 duration. Example: 20240101T120000Z/20240101T130000Z or 20240101T120000Z/PT1H.
RFC 5545 DATE-TIME textual form, typically in UTC with trailing 'Z': YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ. Example: 20231231T235959Z. May also be local or with timezone per spec.
Textual TRIGGER value representation per RFC 5545: either a DATE-TIME (e.g., 20240101T120000Z) for absolute triggers or a DURATION (e.g., -PT15M) for relative triggers.
REQUEST-STATUS property value per RFC 5546/5545 formatted as major.minor;description[;debug]. Example: 2.0;Success or 3.7;Invalid Calendar User;bad cu.

# Generate valid iCalendar PERIOD strings per RFC 5545
# Forms:
#  - <START>/<END>       where START and END are UTC DATE-TIME (YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ)
#  - <START>/<DURATION>  where DURATION is an ISO8601 duration allowed by RFC 5545

# and always return a syntactically valid and interesting period string to seed parsing.

RFC5545_DT_FMT = "%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ"


def _rand_datetime_utc(rng: random.Random) -> datetime:
    # Year range 1970..2169 to match stub
    year = rng.randint(1970, 2169)
    # Choose a valid month/day by constraining via datetime construction
    month = rng.randint(1, 12)
    # Pick a day safely (1..28) to avoid month-length concerns
    day = rng.randint(1, 28)
    hour = rng.randint(0, 23)
    minute = rng.randint(0, 59)
    second = rng.randint(0, 59)
    return datetime(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def _format_dt_utc(dt: datetime) -> str:
    return dt.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime(RFC5545_DT_FMT)


def _rand_duration(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build diverse, valid durations. RFC 5545 supports weeks or days/time components.
    # We generate a mix with optional sign, and combinations of weeks or D/H/M/S.
    neg = rng.choice([False, True])
    use_weeks = rng.choice([True, False])

    if use_weeks:
        weeks = rng.randint(1, 104)  # up to 2 years
        dur = f"P{weeks}W"
    else:
        days = rng.choice([0, rng.randint(1, 30)])
        hours = rng.choice([0, rng.randint(0, 23)])
        minutes = rng.choice([0, rng.randint(0, 59)])
        seconds = rng.choice([0, rng.randint(1, 59)])
        # Construct with allowed omission rules; include T only if any time fields present
        parts = ["P"]
        if days:
            parts.append(f"{days}D")
        if hours or minutes or seconds:
            parts.append("T")
            if hours:
                parts.append(f"{hours}H")
            if minutes:
                parts.append(f"{minutes}M")
            if seconds:
                parts.append(f"{seconds}S")
        # Ensure non-zero duration
        if len(parts) == 1:
            parts.extend(["T", f"{rng.randint(1,59)}S"])  # fallback seconds
        dur = "".join(parts)
    if neg:
        dur = "-" + dur
    return dur


def _rand_start_end_period(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    start = _rand_datetime_utc(rng)
    # Add a positive delta to ensure end >= start
    # Choose from a range spanning seconds to weeks
    delta_choice = rng.randint(0, 5)
    if delta_choice == 0:
        delta = timedelta(seconds=rng.randint(1, 3600))
    elif delta_choice == 1:
        delta = timedelta(minutes=rng.randint(1, 6*60))
    elif delta_choice == 2:
        delta = timedelta(hours=rng.randint(1, 48))
    elif delta_choice == 3:
        delta = timedelta(days=rng.randint(1, 30))
    elif delta_choice == 4:
        delta = timedelta(weeks=rng.randint(1, 12))
    else:
        # mixed components
        delta = timedelta(days=rng.randint(0, 10), hours=rng.randint(0, 23), minutes=rng.randint(0, 59), seconds=rng.randint(1, 59))

def _rand_start_duration_period(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    start = _rand_datetime_utc(rng)

        "20300101T000000Z/P2W",
        # Negative duration relative (allowed by RFC 5545)
        "20240601T080000Z/-PT30M",
        # Start/end equal (zero-length period is valid in some contexts)
        "20250101T000000Z/20250101T000000Z",
    ]
    return rng.choice(candidates)

    sel_mod = rng.randint(0, 2)

        else:

    s = period.encode('ascii')
    if len(s) > 4096:

    return s

def _rand_choice(rnd: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:

def build_datetime_floating(rnd: random.Random) -> str:

    return dt

    if rnd.random() < 0.5:

        hours = _rand_int(rnd, 0, 23)

        time_parts = []
        if hours:
            time_parts.append(f"{hours}H")
        if minutes:
            time_parts.append(f"{minutes}M")
        if seconds or not parts and not time_parts:
            time_parts.append(f"{seconds}S")

            return f"{sign}P{''.join(parts)}T{''.join(time_parts)}"
        else:

    else:

import string
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

# Target: iCalendar TRIGGER value strings for icaltriggertype_from_string
# Valid inputs per RFC5545: either
#  - Absolute DATE-TIME (UTC/Z or local/floating) e.g., 20240101T120000Z
#  - DURATION e.g., -PT15M, P1DT2H, PT0S, P2W
# We also mix in VALUE=DATE-TIME or VALUE=DURATION parameterized content-lines, but
# since the fuzzer stub passes a bare C string (not a full content line), we keep
# to the value itself to maximize acceptance by the parser.

MAX_LEN = 4096

DT_FORMATS_UTC = [
    "%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ",  # Basic format UTC
]
DT_FORMATS_FLOATING = [
    "%Y%m%dT%H%M%S",   # Basic format without Z (floating)
]

# Helper to build a valid ISO-like iCal datetime string

def build_datetime(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Random date within a broad, but reasonable range to avoid overflow
    start = datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    end = datetime(2100, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    delta_seconds = int((end - start).total_seconds())
    sec = rng.randint(0, delta_seconds)
    dt = start + timedelta(seconds=sec)

    # Choose UTC or floating
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        # UTC with Z
        fmt = rng.choice(DT_FORMATS_UTC)
        return dt.strftime(fmt)
    else:
        # Floating time (no Z)
        fmt = rng.choice(DT_FORMATS_FLOATING)
        # Drop tzinfo for formatting correctness
        dt_f = dt.replace(tzinfo=None)
        return dt_f.strftime(fmt)

# Helper to build a valid iCal duration string
# RFC5545 duration grammar examples: PnW | PnYnMnDTnHnMnS | PnDTnHnMnS | PTnHnMnS | PTnS, with optional leading "-"

def build_duration(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    neg = rng.random() < 0.3
    # Choose style: weeks or composite
    use_weeks = rng.random() < 0.2
    parts = []
    if use_weeks:
        weeks = rng.randint(0, 26)  # up to ~half year
        # ensure non-zero duration unless we explicitly choose 0S variant later
        parts.append(f"P{weeks}W")
    else:
        years = rng.choice([0, 0, 0, rng.randint(0, 5)])
        months = rng.choice([0, 0, rng.randint(0, 11)])
        days = rng.choice([0, rng.randint(0, 30)])
        hours = rng.choice([0, rng.randint(0, 23)])
        minutes = rng.choice([0, rng.randint(0, 59)])
        seconds = rng.choice([0, rng.randint(0, 59)])
        # Occasionally generate a pure time duration (PTnM) or pure date (PnD)
        choose_pattern = rng.random()
        if choose_pattern < 0.2:
            # pure seconds
            seconds = rng.randint(0, 3600)
            return ("-" if neg else "") + f"PT{seconds}S"
        elif choose_pattern < 0.35:
            # minutes only
            minutes = rng.randint(1, 300)
            return ("-" if neg else "") + f"PT{minutes}M"
        elif choose_pattern < 0.45:
            # hours only
            hours = rng.randint(1, 72)
            return ("-" if neg else "") + f"PT{hours}H"
        elif choose_pattern < 0.55:
            # days only
            days = rng.randint(1, 30)
            return ("-" if neg else "") + f"P{days}D"
        # Full form
        date_part = "P"
        if years:
            date_part += f"{years}Y"
        if months:
            date_part += f"{months}M"
        if days:
            date_part += f"{days}D"
        time_part = ""
        if any([hours, minutes, seconds]):
            time_part = "T"
            if hours:
                time_part += f"{hours}H"
            if minutes:
                time_part += f"{minutes}M"
            if seconds:
                time_part += f"{seconds}S"
        # Ensure we don't return just "P" with nothing else; fall back to PT0S
        dur = (date_part + time_part) if (date_part != "P" or time_part != "") else "PT0S"
        if dur == "P":
            dur = "PT0S"
        return ("-" if neg and dur != "PT0S" else "") + dur
    s = parts[0]
    return ("-" if neg and s not in ("P0W",) else "") + s

# Sometimes produce a TRIGGER with RELATED=START/END semantics embedded into the value?
# The stub passes only the value string; many libical parsers accept bare duration/datetime.
# To diversify, include leading "+" for positive relative durations occasionally (commonly seen)

def maybe_prefix_plus(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    if s and s[0] != '-' and rng.random() < 0.25 and s.startswith('P'):
        return "+" + s
    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose between duration (relative trigger) and datetime (absolute trigger)
    # Bias slightly toward duration since VALARM commonly uses relative
    kind = rng.choices(["duration", "datetime"], weights=[60, 40], k=1)[0]

    if kind == "duration":
        s = build_duration(rng)
        s = maybe_prefix_plus(rng, s)
    else:
        s = build_datetime(rng)

    # Occasionally add a Z suffix to floating datetimes to force UTC; ensure not already present
    if kind == "datetime" and not s.endswith('Z') and rng.random() < 0.15:
        # Only safe to append if it currently looks like a datetime string without separators
        # If it's already UTC, no change
        s = s + 'Z'

    # Ensure size limit and non-empty
    if not s:
        s = "PT0S"

    b = s.encode('ascii', errors='strict')
    if len(b) > MAX_LEN:
        b = b[:MAX_LEN]
    return b
